Lemma sub_castup_reduct : forall G d e T, sub G d e T ->
  forall B e0, d = trm_castup B e0 -> exists A, reduct B A.
Proof.
  intros G d e T H. induction H; intros Bt et Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - exact (IHsub Bt et Ed).
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - injection Ed as HB _. subst Bt. eexists. eassumption.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - exact (IHsub1 Bt et Ed).
Qed.

Lemma castup_type_shape_gen : forall G d e T, sub G d e T ->
  forall B e0, d = trm_castup B e0 -> (exists A, reduct B A) ->
  (~ (exists p q r, T = trm_prod p q r)) /\ (~ (exists y, T = trm_var_f y)).
Proof.
  intros G d e T H. induction H; intros Bt et Ed Hred.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - exact (IHsub Bt et Ed Hred).
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - (* castup *) injection Ed as HB _. subst Bt. split.
    + intros [p [q [r Hp]]]. rewrite Hp in Hred.
      destruct Hred as [Ax HAx]. apply reduct_prod_inv in HAx; auto.
    + intros [y Hy]. rewrite Hy in Hred.
      destruct Hred as [Ax HAx]. apply reduct_var_f_inv in HAx; auto.
  - discriminate Ed.
  - (* sub_sub *)
    pose proof (IHsub1 Bt et Ed Hred) as [Hnp Hnv].
    split.
    + intros [p [q [r Hp]]].
      destruct (sub_second_prod H0 Hp eq_refl) as
          [[a [b' [c' Ha]]] | [y Hy]].
      * apply Hnp. exists a, b', c'. exact Ha.
      * apply Hnv. exists y. exact Hy.
    + intros [y Hy].
      rewrite Hy in H0.
      apply sub_second_var in H0. destruct H0 as [z Hz].
      apply Hnv. exists z. exact Hz.
Qed.

Lemma sub_castup_prod_false : forall G B e p q r,
  sub G (trm_castup B e) (trm_castup B e) (trm_prod p q r) -> False.
Proof.
  intros G B e p q r H.
  pose proof (@sub_castup_reduct G (trm_castup B e) (trm_castup B e) (trm_prod p q r) H B e eq_refl) as [A HA].
  pose proof (@castup_type_shape_gen G (trm_castup B e) (trm_castup B e) (trm_prod p q r) H B e eq_refl (ex_intro _ A HA)) as [Hnp _].
  apply Hnp. exists p, q, r. reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma progress_any : forall G e1 e2 A,
  sub G e1 e2 A -> e1 = e2 -> value e1 \/ exists t, e1 --> t.
Proof.
  intros G e1 e2 A H.
  induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros Ed.
  - left. apply value_star.
  - left. apply value_ivalue, ivalue_var.
  - left. apply value_ivalue, ivalue_var.
  - exact (IHprem eq_refl).
  - left. apply value_ivalue, ivalue_top.
  - (* abs *)
    left. apply value_abs.
    + exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h1)).
    + exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h2)).
    + apply (@lc_trm_abs L e1 A0 e2).
      * exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h1)).
      * exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h2)).
      * intros x Hx. exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms (hbody x Hx))).
  - (* app *)
    injection Ed as He. subst e2.
    destruct (IH1 eq_refl) as [Hv | [e1' Hs]].
    + destruct Hv as [ | e Hiv | a b c Hlca Hlcb Hlcabs | p q r Hlcp Hlcq Hlcprod | A' e HlcA Hlce ].
      * exfalso. exact (@sub_star_prod_false G0 e3 B C h1).
      * left. apply value_ivalue, ivalue_app.
        -- exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h2)).
        -- exact Hiv.
      * right. exists (open_trm_wrt_trm c A0). eapply reduct_beta.
        -- exact Hlca.
        -- exact Hlcb.
        -- exact Hlcabs.
        -- exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h2)).
      * exfalso. exact (@sub_prod_prod_false G0 p q r e3 B C h1).
      * exfalso. exact (@sub_castup_prod_false G0 A' e e3 B C h1).
    + right. exists (trm_app e1' A0). apply reduct_app.
      * exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h2)).
      * exact Hs.
  - (* prod *)
    left. apply value_prod.
    + exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h6)).
    + exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h3)).
    + apply (@lc_trm_prod L e A0 B).
      * exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h6)).
      * exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h3)).
      * intros x Hx. exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms (h4 x Hx))).
  - (* castup *)
    left. apply value_castup.
    + exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h1)).
    + exact (proj1 (sub_lc_terms h2)).
  - (* castdn *)
    injection Ed as He. subst e2.
    destruct (IH2 eq_refl) as [Hv | [e1' Hs]].
    + destruct Hv as [ | e Hiv | a b c Hlca Hlcb Hlcabs | p q r Hlcp Hlcq Hlcprod | A' e HlcA Hlce ].
      * exfalso. exact (@sub_star_diag_irred G0 A0 h2 (ex_intro (fun X => reduct A0 X) B hr)).
      * left. apply value_ivalue, ivalue_castdn. exact Hiv.
      * exfalso. exact (@sub_abs_diag_irred G0 a b c A0 h2 (ex_intro (fun X => reduct A0 X) B hr)).
      * exfalso. exact (@sub_prod_diag_irred G0 p q r A0 h2 (ex_intro (fun X => reduct A0 X) B hr)).
      * right. exists e. apply reduct_castelim.
        -- exact HlcA.
        -- exact Hlce.
    + right. exists (trm_castdn e1'). apply reduct_castdn. exact Hs.
  - (* sub *)
    exact (IH1 Ed).
Qed.

(* Small facts used by type-well-formedness / right-projection attempts. *)

Lemma sub_star_top_star : forall G, wf G -> sub G trm_star trm_top trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G Hwf. apply sub_top. apply sub_ax. exact Hwf.
Qed.

Lemma sub_top_top_star : forall G, wf G -> sub G trm_top trm_top trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G Hwf. apply sub_top_refl. apply sub_ax. exact Hwf.
Qed.

Lemma sub_star_self_top : forall G e, sub G e e trm_star -> sub G e e trm_top.
Proof.
  intros G e H. eapply sub_sub; [ exact H | ].
  apply sub_star_top_star. apply (sub_wf H).
Qed.

(* A judgement whose second component is [star] can only have a first
   component that is [star] itself or a variable.  This is the dual of
   [sub_star_inv] and is used in the product/codomain case analysis.       *)

Lemma sub_second_star : forall G e A, sub G e trm_star A ->
  e = trm_star \/ exists x, e = trm_var_f x.
Proof.
  intros G e A H.
  remember trm_star as d eqn:Ed.
  revert Ed. induction H; intros Ed; try discriminate Ed.
  - left. reflexivity.
  - right. exists x5. reflexivity.
  - subst e2. apply IHsub1. reflexivity.
Qed.

(* A judgement whose second component is [star] is diagonalizable: the
   only rules producing second component [star] are [sub_ax] and
   [sub_var_trans] (under [sub_sub]), and in both cases the diagonal
   judgement at the same type is derivable.                             *)

Lemma sub_second_star_diag : forall G e A,
  sub G e trm_star A -> sub G e e A.
Proof.
  intros G e A H.
  remember trm_star as d eqn:Ed.
  revert Ed. induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros Ed; try discriminate Ed.
  - apply sub_ax. exact Hwf.
  - apply sub_var_refl with (e := e1); [ apply (sub_wf Hprem) | exact Hb ].
  - subst e2. eapply sub_sub; [ apply IH1; reflexivity | exact h2 ].
Qed.

(* Components of any product that occurs as the first component of a
   judgement are themselves well formed: the domain type is typed at
   [star], the domain term is typed at the domain type, and the codomain
   family is self-typed (cofinitely) in the domain's context.            *)

Lemma sub_prod_components_gen : forall G d e T, sub G d e T ->
  forall p q r, d = trm_prod p q r ->
  (sub G q q trm_star) /\
  (sub G p p q) /\
  (exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p q)
         (open_trm_wrt_trm r (trm_var_f x))
         (open_trm_wrt_trm r (trm_var_f x)) trm_star).
Proof.
  intros G d e T H.
  induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros p q r Ed; try discriminate Ed.
  - (* sub_top *) exact (IHprem p q r Ed).
  - (* sub_prod *)
    injection Ed as He HA HB. subst.
    split; [ exact h3 | split ].
    + exact h6.
    + exists L. exact h4.
  - (* sub_sub *) exact (IH1 p q r Ed).
Qed.

(* Context weakening for the unified judgment, proved by induction on the
   derivation.  The [sub_prod] case builds the well-formedness of the
   extended contexts from the induction hypotheses; the needed self-typing
   of the target domain type follows by first projection ([sub_left]) of
   the source-domain premise.                                             *)

Lemma sub_weaken : forall G t1 t2 T,
  sub G t1 t2 T ->
  forall G', wf G' -> subenv G G' -> sub G' t1 t2 T.
Proof.
  intros G t1 t2 T H.
  induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros G' Hwf' Hsub.
  - (* ax *) apply sub_ax. exact Hwf'.
  - (* var_refl *)
    apply sub_var_refl with (e := e0); [ exact Hwf' | apply Hsub; exact Hb ].
  - (* var_trans *)
    eapply sub_var_trans; [ apply Hsub; exact Hb | ].
    apply IHprem; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
  - (* top *) apply sub_top. apply IHprem; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
  - (* top_refl *) apply sub_top_refl. apply IHprem; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
  - (* abs *)
    apply (@sub_abs (L \u dom G') G' e1 A0 e2 e2' B).
    + apply IH1; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
    + apply IH2; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
    + intros x Hx. apply notin_union_r1 in Hx as HxL.
      apply notin_union_r2 in Hx as HxG.
      apply (IHbody x HxL (G' & x ~ bind_sub e1 A0)).
      * apply wf_cons.
        -- apply IH1; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
        -- apply IH2; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
        -- exact HxG.
      * apply subenv_push. exact Hsub.
    + intros x Hx. apply notin_union_r1 in Hx as HxL.
      apply notin_union_r2 in Hx as HxG.
      apply (IHbstar x HxL (G' & x ~ bind_sub e1 A0)).
      * apply wf_cons.
        -- apply IH1; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
        -- apply IH2; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
        -- exact HxG.
      * apply subenv_push. exact Hsub.
  - (* app *) eapply sub_app; [ apply IH1; [exact Hwf'|exact Hsub] | apply IH2; [exact Hwf'|exact Hsub] ].
  - (* prod *)
    pose proof (sub_left (IH1 G' Hwf' Hsub)) as HA'.
    apply (@sub_prod (L \u dom G') G' e A0 B e' A' B').
    + apply IH1; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
    + apply IH2; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
    + apply IH3; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
    + intros x Hx. apply notin_union_r1 in Hx as HxL.
      apply notin_union_r2 in Hx as HxG.
      apply (IH4 x HxL (G' & x ~ bind_sub e A0)).
      * apply wf_cons.
        -- apply IH6; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
        -- apply IH3; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
        -- exact HxG.
      * apply subenv_push. exact Hsub.
    + intros x Hx. apply notin_union_r1 in Hx as HxL.
      apply notin_union_r2 in Hx as HxG.
      apply (IH5 x HxL (G' & x ~ bind_sub e' A')).
      * apply wf_cons.
        -- apply IH7; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
        -- exact HA'.
        -- exact HxG.
      * apply subenv_push. exact Hsub.
    + apply IH6; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
    + apply IH7; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hsub ].
  - (* castup *) eapply sub_castup; [ apply IH1; [exact Hwf'|exact Hsub] | apply IH2; [exact Hwf'|exact Hsub] | exact hr ].
  - (* castdn *) eapply sub_castdn; [ apply IH1; [exact Hwf'|exact Hsub] | apply IH2; [exact Hwf'|exact Hsub] | exact hr ].
  - (* sub *) eapply sub_sub; [ apply IH1; [exact Hwf'|exact Hsub] | apply IH2; [exact Hwf'|exact Hsub] ].
Qed.

(* Extending a context on the right preserves [subenv], and the packaged
   form of weakening by one fresh binder.                              *)

Lemma subenv_push_right : forall G G' x b,
  subenv G G' -> x # G' -> subenv G (G' & x ~ b).
Proof.
  intros G G' x b H X y c Hy.
  apply binds_push_neq.
  - apply H. exact Hy.
  - intro Hyx. subst y.
    exfalso. apply X.
    apply (get_some_inv (v := c)).
    apply (binds_get (v := c)). apply H. exact Hy.
Qed.

Lemma sub_weaken_push : forall G G' x b t1 t2 T,
  wf (G' & x ~ b) -> subenv G G' -> x # G' ->
  sub G t1 t2 T -> sub (G' & x ~ b) t1 t2 T.
Proof.
  intros G G' x b t1 t2 T Hwf Hsub Hx Hs.
  eapply sub_weaken; [ exact Hs | exact Hwf | apply subenv_push_right; assumption ].
Qed.

(* Right-projection instances for `top' and variable second components. *)

Lemma sub_second_top_diag : forall G e A,
  sub G e trm_top A -> sub G e e A.
Proof.
  intros G e A H.
  remember trm_top as d eqn:Ed.
  revert Ed. induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros Ed; try discriminate Ed.
  - (* var_trans *)
    apply sub_var_refl with (e := e1); [ apply (sub_wf Hprem) | exact Hb ].
  - (* top *) exact Hprem.
  - (* top_refl *) apply sub_top_refl. exact Hprem.
  - (* sub_sub *)
    subst e2. eapply sub_sub; [ apply IH1; reflexivity | exact h2 ].
Qed.

Lemma sub_second_var_diag : forall G e x A,
  sub G e (trm_var_f x) A -> sub G e e A.
Proof.
  intros G e x A H.
  remember (trm_var_f x) as d eqn:Ed.
  revert Ed. induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros Ed; try discriminate Ed.
  - (* var_refl *)
    injection Ed as Hx. subst x5.
    apply sub_var_refl with (e := e0); [ exact Hwf | exact Hb ].
  - (* var_trans *)
    apply sub_var_refl with (e := e1); [ apply (sub_wf Hprem) | exact Hb ].
  - (* sub_sub *)
    subst e2. eapply sub_sub; [ apply IH1; reflexivity | exact h2 ].
Qed.

(* The type in any well-formed binding is itself well formed at [star]. *)

Lemma subenv_refl : forall G, subenv G G.
Proof. intros G y b H. exact H. Qed.

Lemma wf_binds_type : forall G x e A,
  wf G -> binds x (bind_sub e A) G -> sub G A A trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G. induction G as [| G' y b IH] using env_ind.
  - intros x e A Hwf Hb. apply binds_empty_inv in Hb. destruct Hb.
  - intros x e A Hwf Hb.
    destruct b as [eb Ab].
    destruct (@wf_cons_inv G' y eb Ab Hwf) as [Hwf' [He' [HA' HyG]]].
    apply binds_push_inv in Hb.
    destruct Hb as [[Hxy He] | [Hxy Hb']].
    + subst y. injection He as Hbe HAb. subst eb Ab.
      eapply sub_weaken_push; [ exact Hwf | apply subenv_refl | exact HyG | exact HA' ].
    + eapply sub_weaken_push; [ exact Hwf | apply subenv_refl | exact HyG | ].
      eapply IH; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hb' ].
Qed.

(* The *term* in any well-formed binding is self-typed at the binding's
   type.  This complements [wf_binds_type] and is what makes a context's
   stored definitions usable under weakening.                            *)

Lemma wf_binds_sub : forall G x e A,
  wf G -> binds x (bind_sub e A) G -> sub G e e A.
Proof.
  intros G. induction G as [| G' y b IH] using env_ind.
  - intros x e A Hwf Hb. apply binds_empty_inv in Hb. destruct Hb.
  - intros x e A Hwf Hb.
    destruct b as [eb Ab].
    destruct (@wf_cons_inv G' y eb Ab Hwf) as [Hwf' [He' [HA' HyG]]].
    apply binds_push_inv in Hb.
    destruct Hb as [[Hxy He] | [Hxy Hb']].
    + subst y. injection He as Hbe HAb. subst eb Ab.
      eapply sub_weaken_push; [ exact Hwf | apply subenv_refl | exact HyG | exact He' ].
    + eapply sub_weaken_push; [ exact Hwf | apply subenv_refl | exact HyG | ].
      eapply IH; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hb' ].
Qed.

(* A concrete witness that an index-dependent product is a supertype of
   its closed source when the binder's term matches the source domain.     *)

Lemma sub_prod_idx_example : forall x,
  sub (empty & x ~ bind_sub trm_star trm_star)
      (trm_prod trm_star trm_star trm_star)
      (trm_prod (trm_var_f x) trm_star trm_star)
      trm_star.
Proof.
  intros x.
  set (G := empty & x ~ bind_sub trm_star trm_star).
  assert (Hwf : wf G).
  { unfold G. apply wf_cons.
    - apply sub_ax. apply wf_nil.
    - apply sub_ax. apply wf_nil.
    - rewrite dom_empty. apply notin_empty. }
  assert (Hx : sub G (trm_var_f x) (trm_var_f x) trm_star).
  { apply sub_var_refl with (e := trm_star); [ exact Hwf | apply binds_tail ]. }
  assert (Hxs : sub G (trm_var_f x) trm_star trm_star).
  { eapply sub_var_trans; [ apply binds_tail | apply sub_ax; exact Hwf ]. }
  assert (Hax : sub G trm_star trm_star trm_star).
  { apply sub_ax. exact Hwf. }
  apply (@sub_prod \{x} G trm_star trm_star trm_star
                   (trm_var_f x) trm_star trm_star).
  - (* p1 *) exact Hax.
  - (* p2 *) exact Hxs.
  - (* p3 *) exact Hax.
  - (* h4 *) intros y Hy. apply sub_ax.
    apply wf_cons.
    + exact Hax.
    + exact Hax.
    + unfold G; rewrite dom_push, dom_empty; apply notin_union; split; [ exact Hy | apply notin_empty ].
  - (* h5 *) intros y Hy. apply sub_ax.
    apply wf_cons.
    + exact Hx.
    + exact Hax.
    + unfold G; rewrite dom_push, dom_empty; apply notin_union; split; [ exact Hy | apply notin_empty ].
  - (* p6 *) exact Hax.
  - (* p7 *) exact Hx.
Qed.

(* Full component extraction for product subtyping.  Since [sub_sub]
   preserves both terms, any derivation of a product-to-product judgment
   bottoms out in a single [sub_prod] between the very same endpoint
   products, so all the [sub_prod] premises are available for the
   endpoints.  This is used to recover the domain term/type relations and
   the codomain family relation of a product widening.                     *)

Lemma sub_prod_full_gen : forall G d e T,
  sub G d e T ->
  forall p q r p' q' r',
    d = trm_prod p q r -> e = trm_prod p' q' r' ->
    (sub G q' q trm_star) /\
    (sub G p' p q) /\
    (sub G q q trm_star) /\
    (exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
        sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p q) (r ^ x) (r ^ x) trm_star) /\
    (exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
        sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p' q') (r ^ x) (r' ^ x) trm_star) /\
    (sub G p p q) /\
    (sub G p' p' q').
Proof.
  intros G d e T H.
  induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros p q r p' q' r' Ed Ee; try discriminate Ed.
  - (* sub_top: the right component is [top] *)
    discriminate Ee.
  - (* sub_prod *)
    injection Ed as He HA HB. injection Ee as He' HA' HB'. subst.
    split. exact h1.
    split. exact h2.
    split. exact h3.
    split. exists L. exact h4.
    split. exists L. exact h5.
    split. exact h6.
    exact h7.
  - (* sub_sub: terms are preserved *)
    exact (IH1 p q r p' q' r' Ed Ee).
Qed.

(* Codomain-family relation of a product widening, in the target product's
   binder context.  This is the [sub_prod] premise needed to advance a
   codomain family along a widening step.                                  *)

Lemma sub_prod_codom_gen : forall G p q r p' q' r',
  sub G (trm_prod p q r) (trm_prod p' q' r') trm_star ->
  exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
    sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p' q') (r ^ x) (r' ^ x) trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G p q r p' q' r' H.
  destruct (sub_prod_full_gen H eq_refl eq_refl)
    as [H1 [H2 [H3 [H4 [H5 [H6 H7]]]]]].
  exact H5.
Qed.

(* The packaged data of a single product-widening step: domain type and
   term relations, both domain self-typings, the source codomain
   self-typing, and the codomain-family relation in the target binder
   context.  These are exactly the [sub_prod] premises needed to advance
   a codomain family (and hence an opened abstraction body) along one
   step of a widening chain.                                              *)

Lemma sub_prod_step : forall G p q r p' q' r',
  sub G (trm_prod p q r) (trm_prod p' q' r') trm_star ->
  (sub G q' q trm_star) /\
  (sub G p' p q) /\
  (sub G q q trm_star) /\
  (sub G p p q) /\
  (sub G p' p' q') /\
  (exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p q) (r ^ x) (r ^ x) trm_star) /\
  (exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p' q') (r ^ x) (r' ^ x) trm_star).
Proof.
  intros G p q r p' q' r' H.
  destruct (sub_prod_full_gen H eq_refl eq_refl)
    as [H1 [H2 [H3 [H4 [H5 [H6 H7]]]]]].
  split. exact H1.
  split. exact H2.
  split. exact H3.
  split. exact H6.
  split. exact H7.
  split. exact H4.
  exact H5.
Qed.

(* Both binder contexts associated with the two endpoints of a product
   widening are well formed (for a fresh variable), so the target-context
   codomain relation of [sub_prod_step] can be used directly.              *)

Lemma wf_of_prod_step : forall G p q r p' q' r',
  sub G (trm_prod p q r) (trm_prod p' q' r') trm_star ->
  forall x, x # G ->
    wf (G & x ~ bind_sub p q) /\ wf (G & x ~ bind_sub p' q').
Proof.
  intros G p q r p' q' r' H x Hx.
  destruct (sub_prod_step H) as [H1 [H2 [H3 [H6 [H7 [H4 H5]]]]]].
  split.
  - apply wf_cons; [ exact H6 | exact H3 | exact Hx ].
  - apply wf_cons.
    + exact H7.
    + apply sub_left in H1. exact H1.
    + exact Hx.
Qed.

(* Inversion data for a typing of an abstraction pair: regardless of the
   result type (and of [sub_sub] wrappers), the domain term is self-typed
   at the domain type and the domain type is self-typed at [star].  This
   is exactly what is needed to form the body's binder context.            *)

Lemma sub_abs_wf_ctx_gen : forall G d e T,
  sub G d e T ->
  forall a0 D b b',
    d = trm_abs a0 D b -> e = trm_abs a0 D b' ->
    sub G a0 a0 D /\ sub G D D trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G d e T H.
  induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros a0 D b b' Ed Ee; try discriminate Ed.
  - (* sub_top: right component is [top] *)
    discriminate Ee.
  - (* sub_abs: the annotations are forced by the two terms *)
    injection Ed as He1 HD Hb. injection Ee as He1' HD' Hb'.
    subst. split; [ exact h1 | exact h2 ].
  - (* sub_sub: terms are preserved *)
    exact (IH1 a0 D b b' Ed Ee).
Qed.

Lemma wf_abs_body_ctx : forall G a0 D b b' T,
  sub G (trm_abs a0 D b) (trm_abs a0 D b') T ->
  forall x, x # G -> wf (G & x ~ bind_sub a0 D).
Proof.
  intros G a0 D b b' T H x Hx.
  destruct (sub_abs_wf_ctx_gen H eq_refl eq_refl) as [H1 H2].
  apply wf_cons; [ exact H1 | exact H2 | exact Hx ].
Qed.

(* Scope of bindings in a well-formed environment: the free variables of
   the term and type components of every binding lie in the environment
   domain.  This is the key fact that lets a fresh binder name be treated
   as absent from all inherited bindings.                                *)

Definition fvs (G : env) (e1 e2 A : trm) : Prop :=
  forall z, z \in fv_trm e1 \/ z \in fv_trm e2 \/ z \in fv_trm A -> z \in dom G.

Definition fvw (G : env) : Prop :=
  forall x e A, binds x (bind_sub e A) G ->
    forall z, z \in fv_trm e \/ z \in fv_trm A -> z \in dom G.

Lemma fvw_holds : forall G, wf G -> fvw G.
Proof.
  refine (wf_mut
    (fun (G:env) (e1 e2 A:trm) (s : sub G e1 e2 A) => fvs G e1 e2 A /\ fvw G)
    (fun (G:env) (w : wf G) => fvw G)
    _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _).
  - (* sub_ax *) intros G w IHw. split.
    + intros z Hz. simpl in Hz. repeat rewrite in_empty in Hz. tauto.
    + exact IHw.
  - (* sub_var_refl *) intros G y A e w IHw Hb. split.
    + intros z Hz. simpl in Hz. repeat rewrite in_union in Hz.
      repeat rewrite in_singleton in Hz.
      destruct Hz as [Heq | [Heq | HA]].
      * subst z. exact (binds_in_dom Hb).
      * subst z. exact (binds_in_dom Hb).
      * apply (IHw y e A Hb z). right. exact HA.
    + exact IHw.
  - (* sub_var_trans *) intros G y e2 A e1 Hb s IHs. destruct IHs as [IHfvs IHfvw]. split.
    + intros z Hz. simpl in Hz. repeat rewrite in_union in Hz.
      repeat rewrite in_singleton in Hz.
      destruct Hz as [Heq | [He2 | HA]].
      * subst z. exact (binds_in_dom Hb).
      * apply (IHfvs z). tauto.
      * apply (IHfvs z). tauto.
    + exact IHfvw.
  - (* sub_top *) intros G e A s IHs. destruct IHs as [IHfvs IHfvw]. split.
    + intros z Hz. simpl in Hz. repeat rewrite in_union in Hz. repeat rewrite in_empty in Hz.
      apply (IHfvs z). tauto.
    + exact IHfvw.
  - (* sub_top_refl *) intros G A s IHs. destruct IHs as [IHfvs IHfvw]. split.
    + intros z Hz. simpl in Hz. repeat rewrite in_union in Hz. repeat rewrite in_empty in Hz.
      apply (IHfvs z). tauto.
    + exact IHfvw.
  - (* sub_abs *) intros L G e1 A e2 e2' B s IHs s0 IHs0 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar.
    destruct IHs as [IHfvs IHfvw].
    split.
    + intros z Hz. simpl in Hz. set (S := L \u (fv_trm e2 \u (fv_trm e2' \u fv_trm B))).
      destruct (var_fresh S) as [x0 Hx0].
      apply notin_union in Hx0. destruct Hx0 as [Hx0L Hx0r].
      apply notin_union in Hx0r. destruct Hx0r as [Hx0e2 Hx0r].
      apply notin_union in Hx0r. destruct Hx0r as [Hx0e2' Hx0B].
      destruct (IHbody x0 Hx0L) as [HBfvs _].
      assert (L1 : z \in fv_trm e1 -> z \in dom G)
        by (intro H; apply (IHfvs z); tauto).
      assert (LA : z \in fv_trm A -> z \in dom G)
        by (intro H; apply (IHfvs z); tauto).
      assert (L2 : z \in fv_trm e2 -> z \in dom G).
      { intro H2.
        assert (Hop : z \in fv_trm (open_trm_wrt_trm e2 (trm_var_f x0)))
          by (apply fv_open_lower; exact H2).
        assert (Hdom : z \in dom (G & x0 ~ bind_sub e1 A)).
        { apply (HBfvs z). left. exact Hop. }
        rewrite dom_push in Hdom. rewrite in_union in Hdom.
        destruct Hdom as [Heqx | HG].
        - rewrite in_singleton in Heqx. subst z. exfalso. apply Hx0e2. exact H2.
        - exact HG. }
      assert (L2' : z \in fv_trm e2' -> z \in dom G).
      { intro H2.
        assert (Hop : z \in fv_trm (open_trm_wrt_trm e2' (trm_var_f x0)))
          by (apply fv_open_lower; exact H2).

(* Capture-avoiding-free substitution into an environment, used by the
   substitution lemma for the binder that occurs before later bindings.  *)

Definition subst_env (v : trm) (x : var) (G : env) : env :=
  LibEnv.EnvOps.map (subst_binding v x) G.

Lemma dom_subst_env : forall G v x, dom (subst_env v x G) = dom G.
Proof. intros. unfold subst_env. apply dom_map. Qed.

Lemma binds_subst_env : forall G v x y b,
  binds y b G -> binds y (subst_binding v x b) (subst_env v x G).
Proof. intros. unfold subst_env. apply binds_map. exact H. Qed.

Lemma subst_env_empty : forall v x, subst_env v x empty = empty.
Proof. intros. unfold subst_env. apply map_empty. Qed.

Lemma subst_env_push : forall G v x y b,
  subst_env v x (G & y ~ b) = (subst_env v x G & y ~ subst_binding v x b).
Proof. intros. unfold subst_env. rewrite map_push. reflexivity. Qed.

(* Basic computation lemma for substitution into a binding. *)

Lemma subst_binding_eq : forall v x e A,
  subst_binding v x (bind_sub e A) =
  bind_sub (subst_trm v x e) (subst_trm v x A).
Proof. intros. reflexivity. Qed.

(* Substitution is the identity on terms that do not mention the variable. *)

Lemma subst_trm_fresh : forall e v x,
  x \notin fv_trm e -> subst_trm v x e = e.
Proof.
  induction e as [n | y | | | e1 IHe1 e2 IHe2 | e1 IHe1 A IHA e2 IHe2
               | e IHe A IHA B IHB | A IHA e IHe | e IHe | e IHe A IHA ];
  intros v x Hfv; simpl in *.
  - reflexivity.
  - apply notin_singleton_r in Hfv.
    simpl. rewrite If_r. reflexivity.
    intro Heq. apply Hfv. symmetry. exact Heq.
  - reflexivity.
  - reflexivity.
  - apply notin_union in Hfv. destruct Hfv as [H1 H2].
    simpl. rewrite (IHe1 v x H1), (IHe2 v x H2). reflexivity.
  - apply notin_union in Hfv. destruct Hfv as [H1 Hrest].
    apply notin_union in Hrest. destruct Hrest as [HA H2].
    simpl. rewrite (IHe1 v x H1), (IHA v x HA), (IHe2 v x H2). reflexivity.
  - apply notin_union in Hfv. destruct Hfv as [H1 Hrest].
    apply notin_union in Hrest. destruct Hrest as [HA HB].
    simpl. rewrite (IHe v x H1), (IHA v x HA), (IHB v x HB). reflexivity.
  - apply notin_union in Hfv. destruct Hfv as [HA H1].
    simpl. rewrite (IHA v x HA), (IHe v x H1). reflexivity.
  - simpl. rewrite (IHe v x Hfv). reflexivity.
  - apply notin_union in Hfv. destruct Hfv as [H1 HA].
    simpl. rewrite (IHe v x H1), (IHA v x HA). reflexivity.
Qed.

Lemma subst_binding_fresh : forall v x e A,
  x \notin fv_trm e -> x \notin fv_trm A ->
  subst_binding v x (bind_sub e A) = bind_sub e A.
Proof.
  intros. rewrite subst_binding_eq.
  rewrite (@subst_trm_fresh e v x H), (@subst_trm_fresh A v x H0).
  reflexivity.
Qed.

    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb

Every route tried reduces to this composition; no syntactic proof found. Weakening was still a genuine advance (needed by the domain-widening repair).

Next idea if continuing: prove composition and family-context change by a mutual/lexicographic induction on term structure (abs case reduces to body composition when the two codomain families agree; non-injective codomain pairs appear to collapse the terms but this is unproven), or find a verified counterexample. NEW INSIGHT (2026-11-22, corrected): A "realizable target families are closed or the index" invariant is FALSE. `trm_prod (trm_var_b 0) trm_star trm_star` IS realizable as a codomain supertype reached by `sub_prod` from a closed product when the binder type is `star`; e.g. `sub ctx (prod star star star) (prod (var_f x) star star) star` holds because `sub_prod`'s domain premise `sub ctx (var_f x) star star` holds by `sub_var_trans` from `x : star : star`. However, such index families appear to remain COMPARABLE to their sources (`prod star star star <: prod y star star` under `y : star : star`), so the product alignment may still be recoverable. `trm_app (trm_var_b 0) trm_star` does appear unrealizable (infinite regress in the body premise). The unresolved task is to prove the needed comparability/alignment uniformly (or refute it). Still one `Admitted`.

PROOF ARCHITECTURE (2026-11-22, session 3): the beta obligation can be handled by *induction on the function typing's derivation* `hf : sub G f f P`, `P = prod ec Bc Cc`, with the argument premise `Ha : arg : ec : Bc` and goal `body^^arg : Cc^^arg`. The `sub_abs` base is the matching-binder substitution of the diagonal body. The `sub_sub` step `hf = sub_sub hf' htype` is handled by applying the IH at `hf'`'s product after converting the argument typing from `ec:Bc` to `e0:B0` (the source domain) using **same-type transitivity at `B0` with middle `ec`** (both `ec:ec:B0` and `arg:ec:B0` are derivable by `sub_sub` from the chain data), and then the codomain is changed by substituting `arg` into `htype`'s codomain relation (matching binder again). Thus the whole beta case reduces to just TWO core results: (i) matching-binder substitution `sub (G&x~e:A) s t T -> sub G v e A -> sub G sσ tσ Tσ`; (ii) same-type transitivity with self-typed middle `sub G e e A -> sub G v e A -> sub G e c A -> sub G v c A` (used both in substitution's non-diagonal `sub_var_trans` case and in the chain step). No separate chain-collapse/context-change lemma is needed. New verified infra in Task.v: `sub_wf_mut` mutual scheme, `binds_in_dom`, `fv_open_rec_lower/upper`, `fv_open_lower/upper`. Next: prove same-type transitivity with self-typed middle by well-founded induction on the middle term (abs case composes bodies; need to align the canonical codomains, which is where the remaining difficulty is), then substitution, then assemble beta. Still one `Admitted`.

LATEST INSIGHTS (2026-11-22, session 2): (1) `sub_sub` preserves BOTH terms, so any single product/product judgment bottoms out in one `sub_prod` between the exact endpoints ([sub_prod_full_gen]/[sub_prod_step] now prove all seven premises). But a diagonal abs typing at a widened product can pass through INTERMEDIATE product *types*: each `sub_sub` step is a separate product/product judgment, so the type chain must be collapsed (product-transitivity at star) or traversed with a context-change theorem. (2) `sub_top_refl` types `top` at ANY self-typed type `A` (A:A:star), so types that are bare variables (e.g. `var_f y`) ARE inhabited (by `top`); shape intuitions like "no term is typed at a variable type" are FALSE. (3) Shape alignment helps: if `sub G a b A` and `sub G b c A` with `b <> top`, then `a`, `b`, `c` have the same head shape (via term-shape inversion; only `sub_sub`/`sub_top`/`sub_var_trans` can change the type/RHS). This suggests a well-founded induction on the middle term with variable-chain append and abs/abs body composition, but the abs/abs case needs a common codomain type when the two canonical codomains differ yet both widen to the same type; no syntactic closure found. Still one `Admitted`.

content.text:
Added and verified the term/type scope invariant (file compiles; **117 `Qed`**, exactly one `Admitted`, only `Task.v` modified):

- **`fvs_holds`** — for every `sub G e1 e2 A`, the free variables of `e1`, `e2`, and `A` are contained in `dom G`. Proved by structural induction (`sub_ind`), reusing `fvw_holds` in the `sub_ax` / `sub_var_refl` well-formedness cases and the `fv_open_lower/upper` lemmas in the cofinite `sub_abs`/`sub_prod` cases.

Together with `fvw_holds` (binding components) this gives the complete free-variable scope invariant for the judgment and well-formed environments.

Important finding this turn (recorded in-file/memory): this scope invariant is **not** enough to make the naive context-change lemma work. Even when the top-level terms avoid a fresh binder `y`, an inner rule parameter introduced by a cofinite premise (e.g. an inner abstraction's annotation) may mention `y`; scope only places its free variables in `dom (G & y : e : A)`, which includes `y`. Removing/transporting the binder therefore requires substituting or renaming within the whole derivation — i.e. it *is* the substitution lemma, not a simple weakening. So the dependency cycle (substitution → same-type transitivity → context change → substitution) is genuine, and the codomain-alignment/app-composition case still has no syntactic closure. `subject_reduction_wh` remains open; no proof escape or axiom-like shortcut was introduced.

content.thinking:
Let me think about whether the dependency cycle can be broken by proving the substitution lemma and transitivity **mutually with a well-founded measure**, now that we have all the scope/decomposition lemmas. Maybe I can implement a *fuel-based* mutual recursion where the fuel is the size of the term being substituted/involved, avoiding derivation sizes. Let me think about a **term-structural** substitution lemma:

Standard hereditary substitution: define `body[x:=v]` by recursion; the proof of typing preservation by induction on the *body term* structure, using the typing derivation to guide. The hard case is when the body is a variable x which is used non-diagonally at a type... For a *diagonal* body judgment (which is what beta needs), the body derivation is diagonal. The non-diagonal subterms (like sub_app's argument premise) are "type-level" arguments: in sub_app, the argument premise `a:e:B` types the argument a at the domain. When substituting x:=v, we need `aσ:eσ:Bσ`. If a is a variable whose derivation uses x, we need composition. But maybe in a *diagonal* body judgment, the argument term `a` and domain `e` are such that... no.

Let me reconsider the beta proof architecture. Perhaps we don't need the full substitution lemma! We need to instantiate the body at arg. The body typing is available under a *fresh variable* x. Instead of substituting arg, what if we **choose the fresh variable x to be a variable that is later related to arg via the typing of arg**, and use the sub_app rule at the *top level*? Hmm.

Wait. Maybe there's a direct way to type `body^^arg` using the *body typing* and the *typing of arg* without a general substitution lemma, by an induction on the body *term* that only ever substitutes the *same* arg and uses the body typing's diagonal structure. This is hereditary substitution specialized to diagonal typings. The hard case is sub_app's argument premise, but in hereditary substitution we can recursively *type-check* the substituted argument using the typing of arg at the appropriate type. Specifically, the body derivation's sub_app argument premise types a subterm `a` at domain `e`. After substitution, aσ is a term; we need to type it at eσ. If a is exactly the variable x, then aσ=arg and eσ=e; we need arg:e:B — which we have if e3=e and B... but in the widened case the body's domain e might be the canonical d:D, and arg is typed at ec:Bc. The body's sub_app argument premise when a=x is `sub H (var x) e B'`; after subst we need arg:e:B'. We have the premise's derivation! The premise is a *derivation* `sub H (var x) e B'`; substituting x:=arg in this derivation is a substitution instance, but its type is B' and domain e. If e = d and B'=D, we need arg:d:D = arg at the canonical binder; that's the mismatched composition again. So hereditary substitution on a diagonal body still hits the same wall: the body uses x at the canonical binder type, and arg is typed at the widened domain. Unless arg is typed at the canonical binder via the chain verification (Comp). So Comp is unavoidable.

Given that Comp/context-change is genuinely the core, let me try to prove it by **well-founded induction on a measure combining terms and derivations, implemented via a custom `Fixpoint` on the natural number sum of "abstract sizes" where cofinite premises get size 1 plus a bound on their parameters**? The cofinite issue: if we assign size 1 to a cofinite premise, then when we instantiate it at x, the resulting derivation's size isn't bounded by 1. But maybe we don't need to recurse into the instantiated premise with the measure: in a proof by well-founded induction on the *outer* derivation's numeric size, the instantiated premise is a derivation whose size we don't know, so we can't apply the IH. However, we can use the *structural* induction principle `sub_ind`, which handles cofinite premises by giving the IH as a function over x. If our mutual proof is organized as a *mutual structural recursion* over the derivation (using Coq's fixpoint/induction), the cofinite cases are fine. The cross-lemma calls (trans ↔ context change) need to be on derivations that are structural subterms. Are they? In transitivity's product case, context change is applied to D1's h5 and D2's h5' which are *instantiations of cofinite premises* of sub_prod subderivations. Coq's sub_ind gives IHs for cofinite premises as functions `forall x, P (... x ...)`; so if our transitivity induction is on D1 (a sub derivation), the cofinite premises of sub_prod *inside D1* are handled by IH functions. But h5' belongs to D2, not D1. If we do a *mutual structural induction on D1 and D2* (a nested induction: first on D1, then on D2), then when we reach the product case, h5 and h5' are cofinite-premise instantiations from the respective inductions, and we can call context change on them—but context change is a *different lemma*, not one of the two being inducted. If we make context change a third mutually inducted lemma over its derivation (the codomain relation derivation), then its induction is on that derivation, and its cross-calls to transitivity are on... context change's var_trans case needs transitivity on (e'<:e, IH-result), where IH-result is a substituted version of a subderivation, not structural. With both inversions, all three abstractions in the CompSelf abs case yield bodies + canonical codomains + chains to the same A; the remaining issue is aligning the three canonical codomains, which still needs chain composition/context change. Added `subst_trm_fresh` (`x \notin fv e -> subst_trm v x e = e`) and `subst_binding_fresh` (same for `bind_sub`). New: `subst_env` (env map by `subst_binding`) with `dom_subst_env`, `binds_subst_env`, `subst_env_empty`, `subst_env_push` (`subst_env v x (G & y~b) = subst_env v x G & y ~ subst_binding v x b`). Key proved infrastructure (all in Task.v): lc/nb<->open machinery, substitution commutation, `reduct_det`, `reduct_subst`, `sub_wf`, `wf_cons_inv`, `subenv_push`, `sub_lc_terms`, `sub_left`, shape/irreducibility lemmas, `sub_castup_reduct`, `castup_type_shape_gen`, `sub_star/prod/castup_prod_false`, `sub_prod_components_gen` (product components' well-formedness: domain type typed at star, domain term typed at domain type, codomain family self-typed cofinitely in its own domain context), `sub_second_star`, `sub_second_star_diag`, `sub_star_top_star`, `sub_top_top_star`, `sub_star_self_top`, `sub_weaken`, `subenv_push_right`, `sub_weaken_push`, `sub_second_top_diag`, `sub_second_var_diag`, `subenv_refl`, `wf_binds_type` (type of any wf binding is self-typed) (context weakening: `sub G t1 t2 T -> wf G' -> subenv G G' -> sub G' t1 t2 T`, induction with `wf_cons` built from IHs and `sub_left` for the target-domain self-typing).

Remaining obstruction for `subject_reduction_wh`: the beta case needs to instantiate the abstraction body typing at the argument, i.e. same-type composition `sub G u e A -> sub G e v A -> sub G u v A` (and a family-context change `e0 -> e` for codomain self-typing under a changed binding term). In the `sub_app`/`sub_app` case the shared function term is typed at two product types whose domains are a priori unrelated; the shared argument is typed at both domains and only the opened codomains are related by the target. No rule gives a common product/join. `sub_prod_components_gen` gives component well-formedness but does not relate the domains. Opening codomain families is not injective (`trm_var_b 0` vs a self-typed closed term both open to it). `castelim` similarly reduces to type-level coherence under reduction. Every route tried reduces to this composition; no syntactic proof found. Weakening was still a genuine advance (needed by the domain-widening repair).

Next idea if continuing: prove composition and family-context change by a mutual/lexicographic induction on term structure (abs case reduces to body composition when the two codomain families agree; non-injective codomain pairs appear to collapse the terms but this is unproven), or find a verified counterexample. Build with `cd /workspace && make`.

NEW INSIGHT (2026-11-22, corrected): A "realizable target families are closed or the index" invariant is FALSE. `trm_prod (trm_var_b 0) trm_star trm_star` IS realizable as a codomain supertype reached by `sub_prod` from a closed product when the binder type is `star`; e.g. `sub ctx (prod star star star) (prod (var_f x) star star) star` holds because `sub_prod`'s domain premise `sub ctx (var_f x) star star` holds by `sub_var_trans` from `x : star : star`. However, such index families appear to remain COMPARABLE to their sources (`prod star star star <: prod y star star` under `y : star : star`), so the product alignment may still be recoverable. `trm_app (trm_var_b 0) trm_star` does appear unrealizable (infinite regress in the body premise). The unresolved task is to prove the needed comparability/alignment uniformly (or refute it). Still one `Admitted`.

PROOF ARCHITECTURE (2026-11-22, session 3): the beta obligation can be handled by *induction on the function typing's derivation* `hf : sub G f f P`, `P = prod ec Bc Cc`, with the argument premise `Ha : arg : ec : Bc` and goal `body^^arg : Cc^^arg`. The `sub_abs` base is the matching-binder substitution of the diagonal body. The `sub_sub` step `hf = sub_sub hf' htype` is handled by applying the IH at `hf'`'s product after converting the argument typing from `ec:Bc` to `e0:B0` (the source domain) using **same-type transitivity at `B0` with middle `ec`** (both `ec:ec:B0` and `arg:ec:B0` are derivable by `sub_sub` from the chain data), and then the codomain is changed by substituting `arg` into `htype`'s codomain relation (matching binder again). Thus the whole beta case reduces to just TWO core results: (i) matching-binder substitution `sub (G&x~e:A) s t T -> sub G v e A -> sub G sσ tσ Tσ`; (ii) same-type transitivity with self-typed middle `sub G e e A -> sub G v e A -> sub G e c A -> sub G v c A` (used both in substitution's non-diagonal `sub_var_trans` case and in the chain step). No separate chain-collapse/context-change lemma is needed. New verified infra in Task.v: `sub_wf_mut` mutual scheme, `binds_in_dom`, `fv_open_rec_lower/upper`, `fv_open_lower/upper`. Next: prove same-type transitivity with self-typed middle by well-founded induction on the middle term (abs case composes bodies; need to align the canonical codomains, which is where the remaining difficulty is), then substitution, then assemble beta. Still one `Admitted`.

LATEST INSIGHTS (2026-11-22, session 2): (1) `sub_sub` preserves BOTH terms, so any single product/product judgment bottoms out in one `sub_prod` between the exact endpoints ([sub_prod_full_gen]/[sub_prod_step] now prove all seven premises). But a diagonal abs typing at a widened product can pass through INTERMEDIATE product *types*: each `sub_sub` step is a separate product/product judgment, so the type chain must be collapsed (product-transitivity at star) or traversed with a context-change theorem. (2) `sub_top_refl` types `top` at ANY self-typed type `A` (A:A:star), so types that are bare variables (e.g. `var_f y`) ARE inhabited (by `top`); shape intuitions like "no term is typed at a variable type" are FALSE. (3) Shape alignment helps: if `sub G a b A` and `sub G b c A` with `b <> top`, then `a`, `b`, `c` have the same head shape (via term-shape inversion; only `sub_sub`/`sub_top`/`sub_var_trans` can change the type/RHS). This suggests a well-founded induction on the middle term with variable-chain append and abs/abs body composition, but the abs/abs case needs a common codomain type when the two canonical codomains differ yet both widen to the same type; no syntactic closure found. Still one `Admitted`.

content.text:
Added a verified chain inversion lemma (file compiles; **123 `Qed`**, exactly one `Admitted`, only `Task.v` modified):

- `sub_chain_step_inv` — a non-reflexive chain exposes one first widening step and the remaining chain.

Also recorded a promising structural observation about the same-domain chain-collapse problem. For a single widening step `prod e A B → prod e' A' B'`, `sub_prod` yields `A' <: A : star` and `e' <: e : A`: along a chain the domain type and domain term move only *downward* in the subtyping preorder. If a chain starts and ends at the same product `prod d D B`, transitivity would force every intermediate domain type to be mutually related with `D` (and the domain terms likewise), severely constraining a domain drift-and-return. Using this monotonicity to collapse the chain's codomain relations into the base binder context is a concrete next route, but formalizing it (and connecting it to the codomain families) remains nontrivial.

`subject_reduction_wh` is still open; the core obstruction (same-type composition with a self-typed middle, and codomain alignment along widening chains) is unchanged. No proof escape or axiom-like shortcut was introduced.

Let me try to formalize the domain monotonicity for `sub_chain` between same-domain endpoints, and maybe derive something. But `sub_chain`'s intermediate products are not exposed; we'd need a dependent chain type that carries the endpoints' domain data. This is a big detour.

Alternatively, let me revisit the possibility that the whole proof can be done by **strong normalization / semantics encoded via the `sub` judgment's own transitivity at the *level of types***. Hmm.

Let me take a step back and think about whether the benchmark might have a **reference proof using a different, simpler formulation** that avoids our difficulties: perhaps the target theorem `subject_reduction_wh` is only needed for terms `t` that are *closed* (empty context)? No—E is arbitrary. Or perhaps the proof uses the fact that `sub E t t T` with `t` reducible implies `t` is *not* a value, and progress+determinism... no, progress is empty-context only.

What if we can derive `sub E t' t' T` from `sub E t t T` by **`sub_left` + `sub_right`-like reasoning without substitution**, because t' is a *subterm-like* reduct? Beta's reduct body^^arg is not a subterm, but maybe the typing relation is closed under *term-level reduction of the function* in a way that the body's typing is irrelevant? No.

Let me look at the problem from the *reduction* side once more. The beta rule reduces `app (abs e3 A e1) e2` to `open e1 e2`. The typing of the redex via sub_app gives the function typing `sub E (abs..)(abs..) P` and argument typing. If we use `sub_abs_diag_inv`, we get the canonical body typing in ctx x~e3:A and a chain to P. The argument is typed at P's domain. Task: prove `subject_reduction_wh` and `progress_empty_wh` in `/workspace/Task.v` (Ott-generated unified typing/subtyping; TLC; Rocq 9.1). Edit only Task.v; no Admitted/admit/Axiom/Parameter/Abort in the submitted solution; verify with `make` in /workspace.

State as of 2026-11-22 (latest): `progress_empty_wh` is fully proved (via `progress_any`). `Task.v` has 124 `Qed` helper lemmas and exactly one `Admitted` (`subject_reduction_wh`), so the submission is NOT complete. `make` succeeds. Added `sub_chain_single`, `sub_chain_trans`, `sub_chain_step_inv`, and **`sub_prod_same_domain_codom`**: a single product widening `prod d D Bv <: prod d D B` gives `sub (G & x~d:D) Bv^x B^x star` directly (it is exactly `sub_prod`'s h5 in the target=source-domain context). This is the base case for the same-domain chain collapse; the multi-step case still needs domain monotonicity/context handling. INSIGHT on same-domain chain collapse: along a chain product `prod e_i A_i B_i -> prod e_{i+1} A_{i+1} B_{i+1}`, `sub_prod` gives `A_{i+1} <: A_i` and `e_{i+1} <: e_i : A_i`, i.e. domain type and term only move DOWNWARD in the subtyping preorder. If the chain starts and ends at the same `prod d D B`, transitivity would make every intermediate domain type `A_i` equivalent to `D` (and terms mutually related), so drift-and-return is heavily constrained; proving this rigorously (and using it to collapse the codomain relations in the base context) is a promising but nontrivial route. Added `fvw_of_sub`, `fvs_of_sub`, and `sub_fv_dom` (direct scope eliminator). NEW EXPERIMENT: `dependent induction` on the self-typing `Self : sub G e e A` reduces `comp_self` to per-constructor goals of the plain composition statement with the branch's middle-term shape. In the abs branch the type is exactly the canonical product matching the annotation, and both `Hv` and `D` are at that same type, so their `sub_abs_inv` chains start and end with the SAME base domain `e1,A`; what remains is a same-domain chain collapse (`sub_chain G (prod d D Bv) (prod d D B)` implies a relation on `Bv^x, B^x` in ctx `x~d:D`). This is a narrower sub-problem than general context change, but still unresolved. Both free-variable scope invariants are now proved: `fvw_holds` (binding components) and **`fvs_holds`** (`sub G e1 e2 A` implies fv(e1),fv(e2),fv(A) ⊆ dom G; proved by `sub_ind` reusing `fvw_holds` in the `sub_var_refl`/`sub_ax` wf cases). CAUTION on the naive context-change plan: even with both scope lemmas, removing/transporting a fresh binder fails when an *inner* rule parameter (e.g. an inner abs annotation from a cofinite premise) mentions that binder; such parameters are only known to have fv ⊆ dom H. So context change must substitute/rename in the whole derivation, i.e. it is genuinely the substitution lemma, not a simple weakening. Major helpers: **`sub_abs_diag_inv`** (diagonal abs typing -> canonical `B0`, body self-typing in `G & x~d:D`, codomain self-typing, and `sub_chain G (prod d D B0) P`) and **`sub_abs_inv`** (same for two abstractions with the same annotation, returning the non-diagonal body relation). Both proved with `dependent induction H` (needs `From Stdlib Require Import Program.Equality.`, imported). NOTE: in the sub_abs branch, the real body/codomain premises are H1/H3; H2/H4 are extra IHs with awkward equation arguments. With both inversions, all three abstractions in the CompSelf abs case yield bodies + canonical codomains + chains to the same A; the remaining issue is aligning the three canonical codomains, which still needs chain composition/context change. Added `subst_trm_fresh` (`x \notin fv e -> subst_trm v x e = e`) and `subst_binding_fresh` (same for `bind_sub`). Useful fact for the substitution lemma: wf of `G1 & x~e:A & G2` gives `x # G1` and `x # G2`; with `fvw_holds`, bindings in G1 avoid x, so substitution is the identity on G1's bindings and only affects G2's. A `sub_abs_diag_chain` inversion (diagonal abs typing at P yields a chain from its canonical product) is desirable but the remember-based induction is fiddly; the `remember lhs/rhs` gives two linked equations per branch (e.g. `trm_star = rhs` and `rhs = trm_abs d D b`), so one must combine them (`rewrite El in Er` / `subst rhs`) before discriminating. Also added `subst_binding_eq` (unfolding of substitution into `bind_sub`); note `subst_trm_var_f_eq`, `subst_trm_var_f_neq`, `subst_trm_var_b` already existed earlier in the file, so do not duplicate them. New: `subst_env` (env map by `subst_binding`) with `dom_subst_env`, `binds_subst_env`, `subst_env_empty`, `subst_env_push` (`subst_env v x (G & y~b) = subst_env v x G & y ~ subst_binding v x b`). NOTE: `Require Import List` makes unqualified `map` resolve to `List.map`; use `LibEnv.EnvOps.map`. Newest helpers: `sub_wf_mut` (mutual sub/wf induction scheme), `binds_in_dom`, `fv_open_rec_lower/upper`, `fv_open_lower/upper`, `sub_prod_full_gen`, `sub_prod_codom_gen`, `sub_prod_step`, `wf_of_prod_step`, `sub_abs_wf_ctx_gen`, `wf_abs_body_ctx`, `wf_binds_sub`, and **`fvw_holds`**: for every well-formed environment `G`, the term/type components of every binding have their free variables inside `dom G` (proved via the `wf_mut` mutual principle with motive `fvs /\ fvw`; this was the key missing scope fact for a fresh-binder/context argument).

Key proved infrastructure (all in Task.v): lc/nb<->open machinery, substitution commutation, `reduct_det`, `reduct_subst`, `sub_wf`, `wf_cons_inv`, `subenv_push`, `sub_lc_terms`, `sub_left`, shape/irreducibility lemmas, `sub_castup_reduct`, `castup_type_shape_gen`, `sub_star/prod/castup_prod_false`, `sub_prod_components_gen` (product components' well-formedness: domain type typed at star, domain term typed at domain type, codomain family self-typed cofinitely in its own domain context), `sub_second_star`, `sub_second_star_diag`, `sub_star_top_star`, `sub_top_top_star`, `sub_star_self_top`, `sub_weaken`, `subenv_push_right`, `sub_weaken_push`, `sub_second_top_diag`, `sub_second_var_diag`, `subenv_refl`, `wf_binds_type` (type of any wf binding is self-typed) (context weakening: `sub G t1 t2 T -> wf G' -> subenv G G' -> sub G' t1 t2 T`, induction with `wf_cons` built from IHs and `sub_left` for the target-domain self-typing).

Remaining obstruction for `subject_reduction_wh`: the beta case needs to instantiate the abstraction body typing at the argument, i.e. same-type composition `sub G u e A -> sub G e v A -> sub G u v A` (and a family-context change `e0 -> e` for codomain self-typing under a changed binding term). In the `sub_app`/`sub_app` case the shared function term is typed at two product types whose domains are a priori unrelated; the shared argument is typed at both domains and only the opened codomains are related by the target. No rule gives a common product/join. `sub_prod_components_gen` gives component well-formedness but does not relate the domains. Opening codomain families is not injective (`trm_var_b 0` vs a self-typed closed term both open to it). `castelim` similarly reduces to type-level coherence under reduction. Every route tried reduces to this composition; no syntactic proof found. Weakening was still a genuine advance (needed by the domain-widening repair).

Next idea if continuing: prove composition and family-context change by a mutual/lexicographic induction on term structure (abs case reduces to body composition when the two codomain families agree; non-injective codomain pairs appear to collapse the terms but this is unproven), or find a verified counterexample. Build with `cd /workspace && make`.

NEW INSIGHT (2026-11-22, corrected): A "realizable target families are closed or the index" invariant is FALSE. `trm_prod (trm_var_b 0) trm_star trm_star` IS realizable as a codomain supertype reached by `sub_prod` from a closed product when the binder type is `star`; e.g. `sub ctx (prod star star star) (prod (var_f x) star star) star` holds because `sub_prod`'s domain premise `sub ctx (var_f x) star star` holds by `sub_var_trans` from `x : star : star`. However, such index families appear to remain COMPARABLE to their sources (`prod star star star <: prod y star star` under `y : star : star`), so the product alignment may still be recoverable. `trm_app (trm_var_b 0) trm_star` does appear unrealizable (infinite regress in the body premise). The unresolved task is to prove the needed comparability/alignment uniformly (or refute it). Still one `Admitted`.

PROOF ARCHITECTURE (2026-11-22, session 3): the beta obligation can be handled by *induction on the function typing's derivation* `hf : sub G f f P`, `P = prod ec Bc Cc`, with the argument premise `Ha : arg : ec : Bc` and goal `body^^arg : Cc^^arg`. The `sub_abs` base is the matching-binder substitution of the diagonal body. The `sub_sub` step `hf = sub_sub hf' htype` is handled by applying the IH at `hf'`'s product after converting the argument typing from `ec:Bc` to `e0:B0` (the source domain) using **same-type transitivity at `B0` with middle `ec`** (both `ec:ec:B0` and `arg:ec:B0` are derivable by `sub_sub` from the chain data), and then the codomain is changed by substituting `arg` into `htype`'s codomain relation (matching binder again). Thus the whole beta case reduces to just TWO core results: (i) matching-binder substitution `sub (G&x~e:A) s t T -> sub G v e A -> sub G sσ tσ Tσ`; (ii) same-type transitivity with self-typed middle `sub G e e A -> sub G v e A -> sub G e c A -> sub G v c A` (used both in substitution's non-diagonal `sub_var_trans` case and in the chain step). No separate chain-collapse/context-change lemma is needed. New verified infra in Task.v: `sub_wf_mut` mutual scheme, `binds_in_dom`, `fv_open_rec_lower/upper`, `fv_open_lower/upper`. Next: prove same-type transitivity with self-typed middle by well-founded induction on the middle term (abs case composes bodies; need to align the canonical codomains, which is where the remaining difficulty is), then substitution, then assemble beta. Still one `Admitted`.

LATEST INSIGHTS (2026-11-22, session 2): (1) `sub_sub` preserves BOTH terms, so any single product/product judgment bottoms out in one `sub_prod` between the exact endpoints ([sub_prod_full_gen]/[sub_prod_step] now prove all seven premises). But a diagonal abs typing at a widened product can pass through INTERMEDIATE product *types*: each `sub_sub` step is a separate product/product judgment, so the type chain must be collapsed (product-transitivity at star) or traversed with a context-change theorem. (2) `sub_top_refl` types `top` at ANY self-typed type `A` (A:A:star), so types that are bare variables (e.g. `var_f y`) ARE inhabited (by `top`); shape intuitions like "no term is typed at a variable type" are FALSE. (3) Shape alignment helps: if `sub G a b A` and `sub G b c A` with `b <> top`, then `a`, `b`, `c` have the same head shape (via term-shape inversion; only `sub_sub`/`sub_top`/`sub_var_trans` can change the type/RHS). This suggests a well-founded induction on the middle term with variable-chain append and abs/abs body composition, but the abs/abs case needs a common codomain type when the two canonical codomains differ yet both widen to the same type; no syntactic closure found. Still one `Admitted`.

Added a verified monotonicity lemma (file compiles; **125 `Qed`**, exactly one `Admitted`, only `Task.v` modified):

- `sub_prod_domain_relations` — a product widening `prod d D Bv <: prod e A B` at `star` yields `A <: D` and `e <: d : D`, i.e. the domain type and domain term move downward in the subtyping preorder.

This packages the two domain-component premises of `sub_prod` that drive the same-domain chain-collapse analysis.

Status of the target: `subject_reduction_wh` remains open. The verified development now covers the full syntactic metatheory base, both free-variable scope invariants, exhaustive product/abstraction decomposition with widening chains, chain algebra, environment substitution, and domain monotonicity. The unresolved core remains the same-type composition with a self-typed middle; its abstraction branch needs a same-domain chain collapse relating the canonical codomains of the three abstractions in the base binder context, and the chain's intermediate steps move through different binder contexts while their domains are only monotone-comparable. I have neither a syntactic closure nor a verified counterexample, and I have not introduced any proof escape, axiom, or kernel-check shortcut.

Added and verified a type-widening chain lemma (file compiles; **133 `Qed`**, exactly one `Admitted`, only `Task.v` modified):

Definition subenv (G G':env) : Prop :=
  forall x b, binds x b G -> binds x b G'.

Lemma subenv_push : forall G G' x b,
  subenv G G' -> subenv (G & x ~ b) (G' & x ~ b).
Proof.
  intros G G' x b Hsub y c Hy.
  destruct (classic (y = x)) as [Heq|Hneq].
  - subst y. apply binds_push_eq_inv in Hy. subst c.
    apply binds_tail.
  - eapply binds_push_neq; eauto using binds_push_neq_inv.
Qed.

Lemma sub_lc_terms : forall G e1 e2 A,
  sub G e1 e2 A -> lc_trm e1 /\ lc_trm e2.
Proof.
  intros G e1 e2 A H. induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ].
  - split; apply lc_trm_star.
  - split; apply lc_trm_var_f.
  - destruct IHprem as [_ H2]. split; [apply lc_trm_var_f|exact H2].
  - destruct IHprem as [H1 _]. split; [exact H1|apply lc_trm_top].
  - split; apply lc_trm_top.
  - (* abs *)
    destruct IH1 as [He1 _]. destruct IH2 as [HA _].
    split; apply (@lc_trm_abs L); auto.

Task: prove `subject_reduction_wh` and `progress_empty_wh` in `/workspace/Task.v` (Ott-generated unified typing/subtyping; TLC; Rocq 9.1). Edit only Task.v; no Admitted/admit/Axiom/Parameter/Abort in the submitted solution; verify with `make` in /workspace.

State as of 2026-11-22 (latest): `progress_empty_wh` is fully proved (via `progress_any`). `Task.v` has 135 `Qed` helper lemmas and exactly one `Admitted` (`subject_reduction_wh`), so the submission is NOT complete. `make` succeeds. Added `sub_sub_trans`, `sub_abs_self`, and `sub_app_self` (diagonal abstraction/application introduction). NOTE on the app/TComp core: products of the same function term g with codomain openings equal at the shared argument a do appear comparable in examples, and the argument typing at both domains may force the needed domain direction; but this remains unproven. RIGHT-PROJECTION SHORTCUT EXPLORED AND REJECTED: `sub G e1 e2 T -> sub G e2 e2 T` needs `T:T:star` (sub_top). Under that hypothesis base/structural rules and the abs case (using sub_prod_full_gen for the source codomain self-typing) work, but sub_app needs the function product `P:P:star` and castup/castdn need the premise type `A:A:star`; neither follows from the rule premises. So right projection is not a shortcut. Added `sub_top_lift`, `sub_var_top`, `sub_abs_inv_full`, and `sub_prod_self_star` (product type self-typed at star from component facts; regularity ingredient). Regularity of the whole judgment (`sub G e1 e2 A -> sub G A A star`) reduces at sub_app to substituting the argument into the codomain family's self-typing, i.e. again the substitution lemma/CompSelf, so it is not a shortcut around the core. Added `sub_all_lc` (e1,e2,A all lc when A is star-self-typed), `sub_lc_type_star`, and `sub_prod_same_domain_self` (source codomain self-typing of a same-domain widening, in the common binder context; pairs with `sub_prod_same_domain_codom`). IMPORTANT: with both same-domain h4/h5 lemmas, the *single-step* same-domain abstraction composition closes (instantiate both cofinite premises at the same fresh x, use sub_sub plus the body-level composition). Multi-step chains remain blocked: even type-only binder change with the same term and A'<:A still needs the var_trans composition. So progress requires either proving every widening chain can be taken one-step (false in general) or the substitution lemma. CRUCIAL correction: composing two codomain-family relations `B1^x <: B2^x` and `B2^x <: B3^x` CANNOT be done by `sub_sub` (sub_sub changes only the type, preserving the terms). It is term-level transitivity (CompSelf) at star with middle `B2^x`, whose self-typing `B2^x : B2^x : star` is available from `sub_prod_same_domain_self`. So even the two-step same-domain codomain composition reduces to CompSelf and is circular.

COUNTEREXAMPLE HUNT (beta with reduct `star`): if `app (abs e3 A body) star` is typed at a product, then body^^star = star requires body = star or body = var_b 0. Body=star: canonical codomain B0^x types star, so B0 ∈ {star,top}; the chain keeps the target codomain in {star,top}. Body=var_b 0: canonical codomain equals the binder type A, and the chain's first codomain relation forces A ∈ {star,top}; again the chain keeps the target in {star,top}. So the target type cannot be a product, i.e. no counterexample of this shape. Evidence the theorem is TRUE; the syntactic proof still needs the chain induction. Added `sub_prod_domain_relations` (A <: D and e <: d : D for a widening `prod d D Bv <: prod e A B`). Added `sub_chain_single`, `sub_chain_trans`, `sub_chain_step_inv`, and **`sub_prod_same_domain_codom`**: a single product widening `prod d D Bv <: prod d D B` gives `sub (G & x~d:D) Bv^x B^x star` directly (it is exactly `sub_prod`'s h5 in the target=source-domain context). This is the base case for the same-domain chain collapse; the multi-step case still needs domain monotonicity/context handling. INSIGHT on same-domain chain collapse: along a chain product `prod e_i A_i B_i -> prod e_{i+1} A_{i+1} B_{i+1}`, `sub_prod` gives `A_{i+1} <: A_i` and `e_{i+1} <: e_i : A_i`, i.e. domain type and term only move DOWNWARD in the subtyping preorder. BUT domain drift-and-return is REALIZABLE: the two-step chain `prod star star Bv -> prod star top B1 -> prod star star B` is valid (step 1 needs `star <: top` for the domain type; step 2 needs `top -> star` via contravariance plus `star <: star : top` for the term; both domain terms are `star`). The codomain relations live in `y ~ star : top` and `y ~ star : star`, so collapsing them into the base context `x ~ star : star` is a type-changing context transport = substitution lemma. Monotonicity alone does not collapse chains. Added `fvw_of_sub`, `fvs_of_sub`, and `sub_fv_dom` (direct scope eliminator). NEW EXPERIMENT: `dependent induction` on the self-typing `Self : sub G e e A` reduces `comp_self` to per-constructor goals of the plain composition statement with the branch's middle-term shape. In the abs branch the type is exactly the canonical product matching the annotation, and both `Hv` and `D` are at that same type, so their `sub_abs_inv` chains start and end with the SAME base domain `e1,A`; what remains is a same-domain chain collapse (`sub_chain G (prod d D Bv) (prod d D B)` implies a relation on `Bv^x, B^x` in ctx `x~d:D`). This is a narrower sub-problem than general context change, but still unresolved. Both free-variable scope invariants are now proved: `fvw_holds` (binding components) and **`fvs_holds`** (`sub G e1 e2 A` implies fv(e1),fv(e2),fv(A) ⊆ dom G; proved by `sub_ind` reusing `fvw_holds` in the `sub_var_refl`/`sub_ax` wf cases). CAUTION on the naive context-change plan: even with both scope lemmas, removing/transporting a fresh binder fails when an *inner* rule parameter (e.g. an inner abs annotation from a cofinite premise) mentions that binder; such parameters are only known to have fv ⊆ dom H. So context change must substitute/rename in the whole derivation, i.e. it is genuinely the substitution lemma, not a simple weakening. Major helpers: **`sub_abs_diag_inv`** (diagonal abs typing -> canonical `B0`, body self-typing in `G & x~d:D`, codomain self-typing, and `sub_chain G (prod d D B0) P`) and **`sub_abs_inv`** (same for two abstractions with the same annotation, returning the non-diagonal body relation). Both proved with `dependent induction H` (needs `From Stdlib Require Import Program.Equality.`, imported). NOTE: in the sub_abs branch, the real body/codomain premises are H1/H3; H2/H4 are extra IHs with awkward equation arguments. With both inversions, all three abstractions in the CompSelf abs case yield bodies + canonical codomains + chains to the same A; the remaining issue is aligning the three canonical codomains, which still needs chain composition/context change. Added `subst_trm_fresh` (`x \notin fv e -> subst_trm v x e = e`) and `subst_binding_fresh` (same for `bind_sub`). Useful fact for the substitution lemma: wf of `G1 & x~e:A & G2` gives `x # G1` and `x # G2`; with `fvw_holds`, bindings in G1 avoid x, so substitution is the identity on G1's bindings and only affects G2's. A `sub_abs_diag_chain` inversion (diagonal abs typing at P yields a chain from its canonical product) is desirable but the remember-based induction is fiddly; the `remember lhs/rhs` gives two linked equations per branch (e.g. `trm_star = rhs` and `rhs = trm_abs d D b`), so one must combine them (`rewrite El in Er` / `subst rhs`) before discriminating. Also added `subst_binding_eq` (unfolding of substitution into `bind_sub`); note `subst_trm_var_f_eq`, `subst_trm_var_f_neq`, `subst_trm_var_b` already existed earlier in the file, so do not duplicate them. New: `subst_env` (env map by `subst_binding`) with `dom_subst_env`, `binds_subst_env`, `subst_env_empty`, `subst_env_push` (`subst_env v x (G & y~b) = subst_env v x G & y ~ subst_binding v x b`). NOTE: `Require Import List` makes unqualified `map` resolve to `List.map`; use `LibEnv.EnvOps.map`. Newest helpers: `sub_wf_mut` (mutual sub/wf induction scheme), `binds_in_dom`, `fv_open_rec_lower/upper`, `fv_open_lower/upper`, `sub_prod_full_gen`, `sub_prod_codom_gen`, `sub_prod_step`, `wf_of_prod_step`, `sub_abs_wf_ctx_gen`, `wf_abs_body_ctx`, `wf_binds_sub`, and **`fvw_holds`**: for every well-formed environment `G`, the term/type components of every binding have their free variables inside `dom G` (proved via the `wf_mut` mutual principle with motive `fvs /\ fvw`; this was the key missing scope fact for a fresh-binder/context argument).

Key proved infrastructure (all in Task.v): lc/nb<->open machinery, substitution commutation, `reduct_det`, `reduct_subst`, `sub_wf`, `wf_cons_inv`, `subenv_push`, `sub_lc_terms`, `sub_left`, shape/irreducibility lemmas, `sub_castup_reduct`, `castup_type_shape_gen`, `sub_star/prod/castup_prod_false`, `sub_prod_components_gen` (product components' well-formedness: domain type typed at star, domain term typed at domain type, codomain family self-typed cofinitely in its own domain context), `sub_second_star`, `sub_second_star_diag`, `sub_star_top_star`, `sub_top_top_star`, `sub_star_self_top`, `sub_weaken`, `subenv_push_right`, `sub_weaken_push`, `sub_second_top_diag`, `sub_second_var_diag`, `subenv_refl`, `wf_binds_type` (type of any wf binding is self-typed) (context weakening: `sub G t1 t2 T -> wf G' -> subenv G G' -> sub G' t1 t2 T`, induction with `wf_cons` built from IHs and `sub_left` for the target-domain self-typing).

Remaining obstruction for `subject_reduction_wh`: the beta case needs to instantiate the abstraction body typing at the argument, i.e. same-type composition `sub G u e A -> sub G e v A -> sub G u v A` (and a family-context change `e0 -> e` for codomain self-typing under a changed binding term). In the `sub_app`/`sub_app` case the shared function term is typed at two product types whose domains are a priori unrelated; the shared argument is typed at both domains and only the opened codomains are related by the target. No rule gives a common product/join. `sub_prod_components_gen` gives component well-formedness but does not relate the domains. Opening codomain families is not injective (`trm_var_b 0` vs a self-typed closed term both open to it). `castelim` similarly reduces to type-level coherence under reduction. Every route tried reduces to this composition; no syntactic proof found. Weakening was still a genuine advance (needed by the domain-widening repair).

Next idea if continuing: prove composition and family-context change by a mutual/lexicographic induction on term structure (abs case reduces to body composition when the two codomain families agree; non-injective codomain pairs appear to collapse the terms but this is unproven), or find a verified counterexample. Build with `cd /workspace && make`.

NEW INSIGHT (2026-11-22, corrected): A "realizable target families are closed or the index" invariant is FALSE. `trm_prod (trm_var_b 0) trm_star trm_star` IS realizable as a codomain supertype reached by `sub_prod` from a closed product when the binder type is `star`; e.g. `sub ctx (prod star star star) (prod (var_f x) star star) star` holds because `sub_prod`'s domain premise `sub ctx (var_f x) star star` holds by `sub_var_trans` from `x : star : star`. However, such index families appear to remain COMPARABLE to their sources (`prod star star star <: prod y star star` under `y : star : star`), so the product alignment may still be recoverable. `trm_app (trm_var_b 0) trm_star` does appear unrealizable (infinite regress in the body premise). The unresolved task is to prove the needed comparability/alignment uniformly (or refute it). Still one `Admitted`.

PROOF ARCHITECTURE (2026-11-22, session 3): the beta obligation can be handled by *induction on the function typing's derivation* `hf : sub G f f P`, `P = prod ec Bc Cc`, with the argument premise `Ha : arg : ec : Bc` and goal `body^^arg : Cc^^arg`. The `sub_abs` base is the matching-binder substitution of the diagonal body. The `sub_sub` step `hf = sub_sub hf' htype` is handled by applying the IH at `hf'`'s product after converting the argument typing from `ec:Bc` to `e0:B0` (the source domain) using **same-type transitivity at `B0` with middle `ec`** (both `ec:ec:B0` and `arg:ec:B0` are derivable by `sub_sub` from the chain data), and then the codomain is changed by substituting `arg` into `htype`'s codomain relation (matching binder again). Thus the whole beta case reduces to just TWO core results: (i) matching-binder substitution `sub (G&x~e:A) s t T -> sub G v e A -> sub G sσ tσ Tσ`; (ii) same-type transitivity with self-typed middle `sub G e e A -> sub G v e A -> sub G e c A -> sub G v c A` (used both in substitution's non-diagonal `sub_var_trans` case and in the chain step). No separate chain-collapse/context-change lemma is needed. New verified infra in Task.v: `sub_wf_mut` mutual scheme, `binds_in_dom`, `fv_open_rec_lower/upper`, `fv_open_lower/upper`. Next: prove same-type transitivity with self-typed middle by well-founded induction on the middle term (abs case composes bodies; need to align the canonical codomains, which is where the remaining difficulty is), then substitution, then assemble beta. Still one `Admitted`.

LATEST INSIGHTS (2026-11-22, session 2): (1) `sub_sub` preserves BOTH terms, so any single product/product judgment bottoms out in one `sub_prod` between the exact endpoints ([sub_prod_full_gen]/[sub_prod_step] now prove all seven premises). But a diagonal abs typing at a widened product can pass through INTERMEDIATE product *types*: each `sub_sub` step is a separate product/product judgment, so the type chain must be collapsed (product-transitivity at star) or traversed with a context-change theorem. (2) `sub_top_refl` types `top` at ANY self-typed type `A` (A:A:star), so types that are bare variables (e.g. `var_f y`) ARE inhabited (by `top`); shape intuitions like "no term is typed at a variable type" are FALSE. (3) Shape alignment helps: if `sub G a b A` and `sub G b c A` with `b <> top`, then `a`, `b`, `c` have the same head shape (via term-shape inversion; only `sub_sub`/`sub_top`/`sub_var_trans` can change the type/RHS). This suggests a well-founded induction on the middle term with variable-chain append and abs/abs body composition, but the abs/abs case needs a common codomain type when the two canonical codomains differ yet both widen to the same type; no syntactic closure found. Still one `Admitted`.
