Regularity of the whole judgment (`sub G e1 e2 A -> sub G A A star`) reduces at sub_app to substituting the argument into the codomain family's self-typing, i.e. again the substitution lemma/CompSelf, so it is not a shortcut around the core. Added `sub_all_lc` (e1,e2,A all lc when A is star-self-typed), `sub_lc_type_star`, and `sub_prod_same_domain_self` (source codomain self-typing of a same-domain widening, in the common binder context; pairs with `sub_prod_same_domain_codom`). IMPORTANT: with both same-domain h4/h5 lemmas, the *single-step* same-domain abstraction composition closes (instantiate both cofinite premises at the same fresh x, use sub_sub plus the body-level composition). Multi-step chains remain blocked: even type-only binder change with the same term and A'<:A still needs the var_trans composition. So progress requires either proving every widening chain can be taken one-step (false in general) or the substitution lemma. CRUCIAL correction: composing two codomain-family relations `B1^x <: B2^x` and `B2^x <: B3^x` CANNOT be done by `sub_sub` (sub_sub changes only the type, preserving the terms). It is term-level transitivity (CompSelf) at star with middle `B2^x`, whose self-typing `B2^x : B2^x : star` is available from `sub_prod_same_domain_self`. So even the two-step same-domain codomain composition reduces to CompSelf and is circular.

COUNTEREXAMPLE HUNT (beta with reduct `star`): if `app (abs e3 A body) star` is typed at a product, then body^^star = star requires body = star or body = var_b 0. Body=star: canonical codomain B0^x types star, so B0 ∈ {star,top}; the chain keeps the target codomain in {star,top}. Body=var_b 0: canonical codomain equals the binder type A, and the chain's first codomain relation forces A ∈ {star,top}; again the chain keeps the target in {star,top}. So the target type cannot be a product, i.e. no counterexample of this shape. Evidence the theorem is TRUE; the syntactic proof still needs the chain induction. Added `sub_prod_domain_relations` (A <: D and e <: d : D for a widening `prod d D Bv <: prod e A B`). Added `sub_chain_single`, `sub_chain_trans`, `sub_chain_step_inv`, and **`sub_prod_same_domain_codom`**: a single product widening `prod d D Bv <: prod d D B` gives `sub (G & x~d:D) Bv^x B^x star` directly (it is exactly `sub_prod`'s h5 in the target=source-domain context). This is the base case for the same-domain chain collapse; the multi-step case still needs domain monotonicity/context handling. INSIGHT on same-domain chain collapse: along a chain product `prod e_i A_i B_i -> prod e_{i+1} A_{i+1} B_{i+1}`, `sub_prod` gives `A_{i+1} <: A_i` and `e_{i+1} <: e_i : A_i`, i.e. domain type and term only move DOWNWARD in the subtyping preorder. BUT domain drift-and-return is REALIZABLE: the two-step chain `prod star star Bv -> prod star top B1 -> prod star star B` is valid (step 1 needs `star <: top` for the domain type; step 2 needs `top -> star` via contravariance plus `star <: star : top` for the term; both domain terms are `star`). The codomain relations live in `y ~ star : top` and `y ~ star : star`, so collapsing them into the base context `x ~ star : star` is a type-changing context transport = substitution lemma. Monotonicity alone does not collapse chains. Added `fvw_of_sub`, `fvs_of_sub`, and `sub_fv_dom` (direct scope eliminator). NEW EXPERIMENT: `dependent induction` on the self-typing `Self : sub G e e A` reduces `comp_self` to per-constructor goals of the plain composition statement with the branch's middle-term shape. In the abs branch the type is exactly the canonical product matching the annotation, and both `Hv` and `D` are at that same type, so their `sub_abs_inv` chains start and end with the SAME base domain `e1,A`; what remains is a same-domain chain collapse (`sub_chain G (prod d D Bv) (prod d D B)` implies a relation on `Bv^x, B^x` in ctx `x~d:D`). This is a narrower sub-problem than general context change, but still unresolved. Both free-variable scope invariants are now proved: `fvw_holds` (binding components) and **`fvs_holds`** (`sub G e1 e2 A` implies fv(e1),fv(e2),fv(A) ⊆ dom G; proved by `sub_ind` reusing `fvw_holds` in the `sub_var_refl`/`sub_ax` wf cases). CAUTION on the naive context-change plan: even with both scope lemmas, removing/transporting a fresh binder fails when an *inner* rule parameter (e.g. an inner abs annotation from a cofinite premise) mentions that binder; such parameters are only known to have fv ⊆ dom H. So context change must substitute/rename in the whole derivation, i.e. it is genuinely the substitution lemma, not a simple weakening. Major helpers: **`sub_abs_diag_inv`** (diagonal abs typing -> canonical `B0`, body self-typing in `G & x~d:D`, codomain self-typing, and `sub_chain G (prod d D B0) P`) and **`sub_abs_inv`** (same for two abstractions with the same annotation, returning the non-diagonal body relation). Both proved with `dependent induction H` (needs `From Stdlib Require Import Program.Equality.`, imported). NOTE: in the sub_abs branch, the real body/codomain premises are H1/H3; H2/H4 are extra IHs with awkward equation arguments. With both inversions, all three abstractions in the CompSelf abs case yield bodies + canonical codomains + chains to the same A; the remaining issue is aligning the three canonical codomains, which still needs chain composition/context change. Added `subst_trm_fresh` (`x \notin fv e -> subst_trm v x e = e`) and `subst_binding_fresh` (same for `bind_sub`). Useful fact for the substitution lemma: wf of `G1 & x~e:A & G2` gives `x # G1` and `x # G2`; with `fvw_holds`, bindings in G1 avoid x, so substitution is the identity on G1's bindings and only affects G2's. A `sub_abs_diag_chain` inversion (diagonal abs typing at P yields a chain from its canonical product) is desirable but the remember-based induction is fiddly; the `remember lhs/rhs` gives two linked equations per branch (e.g. `trm_star = rhs` and `rhs = trm_abs d D b`), so one must combine them (`rewrite El in Er` / `subst rhs`) before discriminating. Also added `subst_binding_eq` (unfolding of substitution into `bind_sub`); note `subst_trm_var_f_eq`, `subst_trm_var_f_neq`, `subst_trm_var_b` already existed earlier in the file, so do not duplicate them. New: `subst_env` (env map by `subst_binding`) with `dom_subst_env`, `binds_subst_env`, `subst_env_empty`, `subst_env_push` (`subst_env v x (G & y~b) = subst_env v x G & y ~ subst_binding v x b`). NOTE: `Require Import List` makes unqualified `map` resolve to `List.map`; use `LibEnv.EnvOps.map`. Newest helpers: `sub_wf_mut` (mutual sub/wf induction scheme), `binds_in_dom`, `fv_open_rec_lower/upper`, `fv_open_lower/upper`, `sub_prod_full_gen`, `sub_prod_codom_gen`, `sub_prod_step`, `wf_of_prod_step`, `sub_abs_wf_ctx_gen`, `wf_abs_body_ctx`, `wf_binds_sub`, and **`fvw_holds`**: for every well-formed environment `G`, the term/type components of every binding have their free variables inside `dom G` (proved via the `wf_mut` mutual principle with motive `fvs /\ fvw`; this was the key missing scope fact for a fresh-binder/context argument).

Key proved infrastructure (all in Task.v): lc/nb<->open machinery, substitution commutation, `reduct_det`, `reduct_subst`, `sub_wf`, `wf_cons_inv`, `subenv_push`, `sub_lc_terms`, `sub_left`, shape/irreducibility lemmas, `sub_castup_reduct`, `castup_type_shape_gen`, `sub_star/prod/castup_prod_false`, `sub_prod_components_gen` (product components' well-formedness: domain type typed at star, domain term typed at domain type, codomain family self-typed cofinitely in its own domain context), `sub_second_star`, `sub_second_star_diag`, `sub_star_top_star`, `sub_top_top_star`, `sub_star_self_top`, `sub_weaken`, `subenv_push_right`, `sub_weaken_push`, `sub_second_top_diag`, `sub_second_var_diag`, `subenv_refl`, `wf_binds_type` (type of any wf binding is self-typed) (context weakening: `sub G t1 t2 T -> wf G' -> subenv G G' -> sub G' t1 t2 T`, induction with `wf_cons` built from IHs and `sub_left` for the target-domain self-typing).

Remaining obstruction for `subject_reduction_wh`: the beta case needs to instantiate the abstraction body typing at the argument, i.e. same-type composition `sub G u e A -> sub G e v A -> sub G u v A` (and a family-context change `e0 -> e` for codomain self-typing under a changed binding term). In the `sub_app`/`sub_app` case the shared function term is typed at two product types whose domains are a priori unrelated; the shared argument is typed at both domains and only the opened codomains are related by the target. No rule gives a common product/join. `sub_prod_components_gen` gives component well-formedness but does not relate the domains. Opening codomain families is not injective (`trm_var_b 0` vs a self-typed closed term both open to it). `castelim` similarly reduces to type-level coherence under reduction. Every route tried reduces to this composition; no syntactic proof found. Weakening was still a genuine advance (needed by the domain-widening repair).

Next idea if continuing: prove composition and family-context change by a mutual/lexicographic induction on term structure (abs case reduces to body composition when the two codomain families agree; non-injective codomain pairs appear to collapse the terms but this is unproven), or find a verified counterexample. Build with `cd /workspace && make`.

NEW INSIGHT (2026-11-22, corrected): A "realizable target families are closed or the index" invariant is FALSE. `trm_prod (trm_var_b 0) trm_star trm_star` IS realizable as a codomain supertype reached by `sub_prod` from a closed product when the binder type is `star`; e.g. `sub ctx (prod star star star) (prod (var_f x) star star) star` holds because `sub_prod`'s domain premise `sub ctx (var_f x) star star` holds by `sub_var_trans` from `x : star : star`. However, such index families appear to remain COMPARABLE to their sources (`prod star star star <: prod y star star` under `y : star : star`), so the product alignment may still be recoverable. `trm_app (trm_var_b 0) trm_star` does appear unrealizable (infinite regress in the body premise). The unresolved task is to prove the needed comparability/alignment uniformly (or refute it). Still one `Admitted`.

PROOF ARCHITECTURE (2026-11-22, session 3): the beta obligation can be handled by *induction on the function typing's derivation* `hf : sub G f f P`, `P = prod ec Bc Cc`, with the argument premise `Ha : arg : ec : Bc` and goal `body^^arg : Cc^^arg`. The `sub_abs` base is the matching-binder substitution of the diagonal body. The `sub_sub` step `hf = sub_sub hf' htype` is handled by applying the IH at `hf'`'s product after converting the argument typing from `ec:Bc` to `e0:B0` (the source domain) using **same-type transitivity at `B0` with middle `ec`** (both `ec:ec:B0` and `arg:ec:B0` are derivable by `sub_sub` from the chain data), and then the codomain is changed by substituting `arg` into `htype`'s codomain relation (matching binder again). Thus the whole beta case reduces to just TWO core results: (i) matching-binder substitution `sub (G&x~e:A) s t T -> sub G v e A -> sub G sσ tσ Tσ`; (ii) same-type transitivity with self-typed middle `sub G e e A -> sub G v e A -> sub G e c A -> sub G v c A` (used both in substitution's non-diagonal `sub_var_trans` case and in the chain step). No separate chain-collapse/context-change lemma is needed. New verified infra in Task.v: `sub_wf_mut` mutual scheme, `binds_in_dom`, `fv_open_rec_lower/upper`, `fv_open_lower/upper`. Next: prove same-type transitivity with self-typed middle by well-founded induction on the middle term (abs case composes bodies; need to align the canonical codomains, which is where the remaining difficulty is), then substitution, then assemble beta. Still one `Admitted`.

LATEST INSIGHTS (2026-11-22, session 2): (1) `sub_sub` preserves BOTH terms, so any single product/product judgment bottoms out in one `sub_prod` between the exact endpoints ([sub_prod_full_gen]/[sub_prod_step] now prove all seven premises). But a diagonal abs typing at a widened product can pass through INTERMEDIATE product *types*: each `sub_sub` step is a separate product/product judgment, so the type chain must be collapsed (product-transitivity at star) or traversed with a context-change theorem. (2) `sub_top_refl` types `top` at ANY self-typed type `A` (A:A:star), so types that are bare variables (e.g. `var_f y`) ARE inhabited (by `top`); shape intuitions like "no term is typed at a variable type" are FALSE. (3) Shape alignment helps: if `sub G a b A` and `sub G b c A` with `b <> top`, then `a`, `b`, `c` have the same head shape (via term-shape inversion; only `sub_sub`/`sub_top`/`sub_var_trans` can change the type/RHS). This suggests a well-founded induction on the middle term with variable-chain append and abs/abs body composition, but the abs/abs case needs a common codomain type when the two canonical codomains differ yet both widen to the same type; no syntactic closure found. Still one `Admitted`.

The variable-middle case also has a type-mismatch sub-case (different binding types along a variable chain), so it is not immediate. Added substitution-distribution lemmas for all term constructors and **`sub_chain_lift`**: for a chain `P →* Q`, any judgment `sub G s t P` lifts to `sub G s t Q` (replays `sub_sub` along the chain). This does NOT directly give the beta goal at `Cc^^arg`: the chain's steps are between product *types*, while the goal type is an opening of the target codomain, so one still needs to substitute the argument into each step's codomain relation (matching binder, requiring the domain-conversion CompSelf). Added `sub_sub_trans`, `sub_abs_self`, and `sub_app_self` (diagonal abstraction/application introduction). NOTE on the app/TComp core: products of the same function term g with codomain openings equal at the shared argument a do appear comparable in examples, and the argument typing at both domains may force the needed domain direction; but this remains unproven. RIGHT-PROJECTION SHORTCUT EXPLORED AND REJECTED: `sub G e1 e2 T -> sub G e2 e2 T` needs `T:T:star` (sub_top). Under that hypothesis base/structural rules and the abs case (using sub_prod_full_gen for the source codomain self-typing) work, but sub_app needs the function product `P:P:star` and castup/castdn need the premise type `A:A:star`; neither follows from the rule premises. So right projection is not a shortcut. Added `sub_top_lift`, `sub_var_top`, `sub_abs_inv_full`, and `sub_prod_self_star` (product type self-typed at star from component facts; regularity ingredient). Regularity of the whole judgment (`sub G e1 e2 A -> sub G A A star`) reduces at sub_app to substituting the argument into the codomain family's self-typing, i.e. again the substitution lemma/CompSelf, so it is not a shortcut around the core. Added `sub_all_lc` (e1,e2,A all lc when A is star-self-typed), `sub_lc_type_star`, and `sub_prod_same_domain_self` (source codomain self-typing of a same-domain widening, in the common binder context; pairs with `sub_prod_same_domain_codom`). IMPORTANT: with both same-domain h4/h5 lemmas, the *single-step* same-domain abstraction composition closes (instantiate both cofinite premises at the same fresh x, use sub_sub plus the body-level composition). Multi-step chains remain blocked: even type-only binder change with the same term and A'<:A still needs the var_trans composition. So progress requires either proving every widening chain can be taken one-step (false in general) or the substitution lemma. CRUCIAL correction: composing two codomain-family relations `B1^x <: B2^x` and `B2^x <: B3^x` CANNOT be done by `sub_sub` (sub_sub changes only the type, preserving the terms). It is term-level transitivity (CompSelf) at star with middle `B2^x`, whose self-typing `B2^x : B2^x : star` is available from `sub_prod_same_domain_self`. So even the two-step same-domain codomain composition reduces to CompSelf and is circular.

COUNTEREXAMPLE HUNT (beta with reduct `star`): if `app (abs e3 A body) star` is typed at a product, then body^^star = star requires body = star or body = var_b 0. Body=star: canonical codomain B0^x types star, so B0 ∈ {star,top}; the chain keeps the target codomain in {star,top}. Body=var_b 0: canonical codomain equals the binder type A, and the chain's first codomain relation forces A ∈ {star,top}; again the chain keeps the target in {star,top}. So the target type cannot be a product, i.e. no counterexample of this shape. Evidence the theorem is TRUE; the syntactic proof still needs the chain induction. Added `sub_prod_domain_relations` (A <: D and e <: d : D for a widening `prod d D Bv <: prod e A B`). Added `sub_chain_single`, `sub_chain_trans`, `sub_chain_step_inv`, and **`sub_prod_same_domain_codom`**: a single product widening `prod d D Bv <: prod d D B` gives `sub (G & x~d:D) Bv^x B^x star` directly (it is exactly `sub_prod`'s h5 in the target=source-domain context). This is the base case for the same-domain chain collapse; the multi-step case still needs domain monotonicity/context handling. INSIGHT on same-domain chain collapse: along a chain product `prod e_i A_i B_i -> prod e_{i+1} A_{i+1} B_{i+1}`, `sub_prod` gives `A_{i+1} <: A_i` and `e_{i+1} <: e_i : A_i`, i.e. domain type and term only move DOWNWARD in the subtyping preorder. BUT domain drift-and-return is REALIZABLE: the two-step chain `prod star star Bv -> prod star top B1 -> prod star star B` is valid (step 1 needs `star <: top` for the domain type; step 2 needs `top -> star` via contravariance plus `star <: star : top` for the term; both domain terms are `star`). The codomain relations live in `y ~ star : top` and `y ~ star : star`, so collapsing them into the base context `x ~ star : star` is a type-changing context transport = substitution lemma. Monotonicity alone does not collapse chains. Added `fvw_of_sub`, `fvs_of_sub`, and `sub_fv_dom` (direct scope eliminator). NEW EXPERIMENT: `dependent induction` on the self-typing `Self : sub G e e A` reduces `comp_self` to per-constructor goals of the plain composition statement with the branch's middle-term shape. In the abs branch the type is exactly the canonical product matching the annotation, and both `Hv` and `D` are at that same type, so their `sub_abs_inv` chains start and end with the SAME base domain `e1,A`; what remains is a same-domain chain collapse (`sub_chain G (prod d D Bv) (prod d D B)` implies a relation on `Bv^x, B^x` in ctx `x~d:D`). This is a narrower sub-problem than general context change, but still unresolved. Both free-variable scope invariants are now proved: `fvw_holds` (binding components) and **`fvs_holds`** (`sub G e1 e2 A` implies fv(e1),fv(e2),fv(A) ⊆ dom G; proved by `sub_ind` reusing `fvw_holds` in the `sub_var_refl`/`sub_ax` wf cases). CAUTION on the naive context-change plan: even with both scope lemmas, removing/transporting a fresh binder fails when an *inner* rule parameter (e.g. an inner abs annotation from a cofinite premise) mentions that binder; such parameters are only known to have fv ⊆ dom H. So context change must substitute/rename in the whole derivation, i.e. it is genuinely the substitution lemma, not a simple weakening. Major helpers: **`sub_abs_diag_inv`** (diagonal abs typing -> canonical `B0`, body self-typing in `G & x~d:D`, codomain self-typing, and `sub_chain G (prod d D B0) P`) and **`sub_abs_inv`** (same for two abstractions with the same annotation, returning the non-diagonal body relation). Both proved with `dependent induction H` (needs `From Stdlib Require Import Program.Equality.`, imported). NOTE: in the sub_abs branch, the real body/codomain premises are H1/H3; H2/H4 are extra IHs with awkward equation arguments. With both inversions, all three abstractions in the CompSelf abs case yield bodies + canonical codomains + chains to the same A; the remaining issue is aligning the three canonical codomains, which still needs chain composition/context change. Added `subst_trm_fresh` (`x \notin fv e -> subst_trm v x e = e`) and `subst_binding_fresh` (same for `bind_sub`). Useful fact for the substitution lemma: wf of `G1 & x~e:A & G2` gives `x # G1` and `x # G2`; with `fvw_holds`, bindings in G1 avoid x, so substitution is the identity on G1's bindings and only affects G2's. A `sub_abs_diag_chain` inversion (diagonal abs typing at P yields a chain from its canonical product) is desirable but the remember-based induction is fiddly; the `remember lhs/rhs` gives two linked equations per branch (e.g. `trm_star = rhs` and `rhs = trm_abs d D b`), so one must combine them (`rewrite El in Er` / `subst rhs`) before discriminating. Also added `subst_binding_eq` (unfolding of substitution into `bind_sub`); note `subst_trm_var_f_eq`, `subst_trm_var_f_neq`, `subst_trm_var_b` already existed earlier in the file, so do not duplicate them. New: `subst_env` (env map by `subst_binding`) with `dom_subst_env`, `binds_subst_env`, `subst_env_empty`, `subst_env_push` (`subst_env v x (G & y~b) = subst_env v x G & y ~ subst_binding v x b`). NOTE: `Require Import List` makes unqualified `map` resolve to `List.map`; use `LibEnv.EnvOps.map`. Remaining obstruction for `subject_reduction_wh`: the beta case needs to instantiate the abstraction body typing at the argument, i.e. same-type composition `sub G u e A -> sub G e v A -> sub G u v A` (and a family-context change `e0 -> e` for codomain self-typing under a changed binding term). In the `sub_app`/`sub_app` case the shared function term is typed at two product types whose domains are a priori unrelated; the shared argument is typed at both domains and only the opened codomains are related by the target. No rule gives a common product/join. `sub_prod_components_gen` gives component well-formedness but does not relate the domains. Opening codomain families is not injective (`trm_var_b 0` vs a self-typed closed term both open to it). `castelim` similarly reduces to type-level coherence under reduction. Every route tried reduces to this composition; no syntactic proof found. Weakening was still a genuine advance (needed by the domain-widening repair).

Next idea if continuing: prove composition and family-context change by a mutual/lexicographic induction on term structure (abs case reduces to body composition when the two codomain families agree; non-injective codomain pairs appear to collapse the terms but this is unproven), or find a verified counterexample. NEW INSIGHT (2026-11-22, corrected): A "realizable target families are closed or the index" invariant is FALSE. `trm_prod (trm_var_b 0) trm_star trm_star` IS realizable as a codomain supertype reached by `sub_prod` from a closed product when the binder type is `star`; e.g. `sub ctx (prod star star star) (prod (var_f x) star star) star` holds because `sub_prod`'s domain premise `sub ctx (var_f x) star star` holds by `sub_var_trans` from `x : star : star`. However, such index families appear to remain COMPARABLE to their sources (`prod star star star <: prod y star star` under `y : star : star`), so the product alignment may still be recoverable. `trm_app (trm_var_b 0) trm_star` does appear unrealizable (infinite regress in the body premise). The unresolved task is to prove the needed comparability/alignment uniformly (or refute it). Still one `Admitted`.

PROOF ARCHITECTURE (2026-11-22, session 3): the beta obligation can be handled by *induction on the function typing's derivation* `hf : sub G f f P`, `P = prod ec Bc Cc`, with the argument premise `Ha : arg : ec : Bc` and goal `body^^arg : Cc^^arg`. The `sub_abs` base is the matching-binder substitution of the diagonal body. The `sub_sub` step `hf = sub_sub hf' htype` is handled by applying the IH at `hf'`'s product after converting the argument typing from `ec:Bc` to `e0:B0` (the source domain) using **same-type transitivity at `B0` with middle `ec`** (both `ec:ec:B0` and `arg:ec:B0` are derivable by `sub_sub` from the chain data), and then the codomain is changed by substituting `arg` into `htype`'s codomain relation (matching binder again). Thus the whole beta case reduces to just TWO core results: (i) matching-binder substitution `sub (G&x~e:A) s t T -> sub G v e A -> sub G sσ tσ Tσ`; (ii) same-type transitivity with self-typed middle `sub G e e A -> sub G v e A -> sub G e c A -> sub G v c A` (used both in substitution's non-diagonal `sub_var_trans` case and in the chain step). No separate chain-collapse/context-change lemma is needed. New verified infra in Task.v: `sub_wf_mut` mutual scheme, `binds_in_dom`, `fv_open_rec_lower/upper`, `fv_open_lower/upper`. Next: prove same-type transitivity with self-typed middle by well-founded induction on the middle term (abs case composes bodies; need to align the canonical codomains, which is where the remaining difficulty is), then substitution, then assemble beta. Still one `Admitted`.

LATEST INSIGHTS (2026-11-22, session 2): (1) `sub_sub` preserves BOTH terms, so any single product/product judgment bottoms out in one `sub_prod` between the exact endpoints ([sub_prod_full_gen]/[sub_prod_step] now prove all seven premises). But a diagonal abs typing at a widened product can pass through INTERMEDIATE product *types*: each `sub_sub` step is a separate product/product judgment, so the type chain must be collapsed (product-transitivity at star) or traversed with a context-change theorem. (2) `sub_top_refl` types `top` at ANY self-typed type `A` (A:A:star), so types that are bare variables (e.g. `var_f y`) ARE inhabited (by `top`); shape intuitions like "no term is typed at a variable type" are FALSE. (3) Shape alignment helps: if `sub G a b A` and `sub G b c A` with `b <> top`, then `a`, `b`, `c` have the same head shape (via term-shape inversion; only `sub_sub`/`sub_top`/`sub_var_trans` can change the type/RHS). This suggests a well-founded induction on the middle term with variable-chain append and abs/abs body composition, but the abs/abs case needs a common codomain type when the two canonical codomains differ yet both widen to the same type; no syntactic closure found. Still one `Admitted`.

(* General abstraction introduction (specialized [sub_abs] naming). *)

Lemma sub_abs_intro : forall L G d D b1 b2 B,
  sub G d d D -> sub G D D trm_star ->
  (forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (b1 ^ x) (b2 ^ x) (B ^ x)) ->
  (forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (B ^ x) (B ^ x) trm_star) ->
  sub G (trm_abs d D b1) (trm_abs d D b2) (trm_prod d D B).
Proof.
  intros L G d D b1 b2 B Hd HD Hb Hc.
  apply (sub_abs L G d D b1 b2 B); assumption.
Qed.

(* Diagonal cast introduction rules. *)

Lemma sub_castup_self : forall G B e A,
  sub G B B trm_star -> sub G e e A -> reduct B A ->
  sub G (trm_castup B e) (trm_castup B e) B.
Proof.
  intros G B e A HB He hr.
  apply (sub_castup G B e e A); assumption.
Qed.

Lemma sub_castdn_self : forall G e B A,
  sub G B B trm_star -> sub G e e A -> reduct A B ->
  sub G (trm_castdn e) (trm_castdn e) B.
Proof.
  intros G e B A HB He hr.
  apply (sub_castdn G e e B A); assumption.
Qed.

(* Canonical castelim coherence: the term-level reduction determines the
   type up to [reduct_det].                                              *)

Lemma castelim_subject : forall G B e A T,
  sub G B B trm_star -> sub G e e A -> reduct B A ->
  sub G T T trm_star -> reduct B T ->
  sub G e e T.
Proof.
  intros G B e A T HB He hrA HT hrT.
  assert (A = T) as Heq by (eapply reduct_det; [ exact hrA | exact hrT ]).
  subst T. exact He.
Qed.

(* Same-type transitivity with a self-typed middle, for the atomic middle
   terms [top] and [star].                                              *)

Lemma comp_self_top : forall G A,
  sub G trm_top trm_top A ->
  forall v, sub G v trm_top A ->
  forall c, sub G trm_top c A -> sub G v c A.
Proof.
  intros G A Self v Hv c D.
  apply sub_top_inv in D. subst c. exact Hv.
Qed.

Lemma comp_self_star : forall G A,
  sub G trm_star trm_star A ->
  forall v, sub G v trm_star A ->
  forall c, sub G trm_star c A -> sub G v c A.
Proof.
  intros G A Self v Hv c D.
  pose proof (sub_star_type_shape Self) as HA.
  destruct HA as [HA | HA]; subst A.
  - pose proof (sub_star_inv D) as HD.
    destruct HD as [-> | ->].
    + exact Hv.
    + apply sub_top. apply sub_left in Hv. exact Hv.
  - pose proof (sub_star_inv D) as HD.
    destruct HD as [-> | ->].
    + exact Hv.
    + apply sub_top. apply sub_left in Hv. exact Hv.
Qed.

(* CompSelf at the coarse type suffices for the form where the self-typing
   is given at a finer type related by a widening (the [sub_sub] shape).  *)

Lemma comp_gen_of_comp_self :
  (forall G e A, sub G e e A ->
     forall v, sub G v e A -> forall c, sub G e c A -> sub G v c A) ->
  forall G e A0 A,
    sub G e e A0 -> sub G A0 A trm_star ->
    forall v, sub G v e A ->
    forall c, sub G e c A -> sub G v c A.
Proof.
  intros Hcomp G e A0 A Self0 h v Hv c D.
  apply (Hcomp G e A).
  - eapply sub_sub; [ exact Self0 | exact h ].
  - exact Hv.
  - exact D.
Qed.

(* A typing of a variable term at a variable right-hand side exposes a
   binding variable plus a chain from that binding's type to the result
   type.  (All non-variable-right rules are eliminated.)                 *)

Lemma var_typing_chain : forall G v y A,
  sub G v (trm_var_f y) A ->
  exists z e_z A_z,
    v = trm_var_f z /\ binds z (bind_sub e_z A_z) G /\ sub_chain G A_z A.
Proof.
  intros G v y A H.
  dependent induction H.
  - (* var_refl *)
    exists y, e, A. split; [reflexivity|split; [exact H0|apply sub_chain_refl]].
  - (* var_trans *)
    exists x5, e1, A. split; [reflexivity|split; [exact H|apply sub_chain_refl]].
  - (* sub_sub *)
    destruct (IHsub1 y eq_refl) as [z [ez [Az [Hv [Hb Hc]]]]].
    exists z, ez, Az. split; [exact Hv|split; [exact Hb|]].
    eapply sub_chain_append; [exact Hc | exact H0].
Qed.

(* Variable-target base extraction: every typing of a variable right-hand
   side reaches the result type from that variable's own binding type by a
   chain.                                                               *)

Lemma var_target_base : forall G v y A,
  sub G v (trm_var_f y) A ->
  exists e_y A_y, binds y (bind_sub e_y A_y) G /\ sub_chain G A_y A.
Proof.

Definition subenv (G G':env) : Prop :=
  forall x b, binds x b G -> binds x b G'.

Lemma subenv_push : forall G G' x b,
  subenv G G' -> subenv (G & x ~ b) (G' & x ~ b).
Proof.
  intros G G' x b Hsub y c Hy.
  destruct (classic (y = x)) as [Heq|Hneq].
  - subst y. apply binds_push_eq_inv in Hy. subst c.
    apply binds_tail.
  - eapply binds_push_neq; eauto using binds_push_neq_inv.
Qed.

Lemma sub_lc_terms : forall G e1 e2 A,
  sub G e1 e2 A -> lc_trm e1 /\ lc_trm e2.
Proof.
  intros G e1 e2 A H. induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ].
  - split; apply lc_trm_star.
  - split; apply lc_trm_var_f.
  - destruct IHprem as [_ H2]. split; [apply lc_trm_var_f|exact H2].
  - destruct IHprem as [H1 _]. split; [exact H1|apply lc_trm_top].
  - split; apply lc_trm_top.
  - (* abs *)
    destruct IH1 as [He1 _]. destruct IH2 as [HA _].
    split; apply (@lc_trm_abs L); auto.
    + intros x Hx. apply (proj1 (IHbody x Hx)).
    + intros x Hx. apply (proj2 (IHbody x Hx)).
  - (* app *)
    destruct IH1 as [He1 He2]. destruct IH2 as [HA _].
    split; apply lc_trm_app; auto.
  - (* prod *)
    destruct IH1 as [HA' HA].
    destruct IH2 as [He' He].
    destruct IH7 as [He'2 _].
    split.
    + apply (@lc_trm_prod L); auto.
      intros x Hx. apply (proj1 (IH4 x Hx)).
    + apply (@lc_trm_prod L); auto.
      intros x Hx. apply (proj2 (IH5 x Hx)).
  - (* castup *)
    destruct IH1 as [HB _]. destruct IH2 as [He1 He2].
    split; apply lc_trm_castup; auto.
  - (* castdn *)
    destruct IH2 as [He1 He2].
    split; [apply lc_trm_castdn; exact He1 | apply lc_trm_castdn; exact He2].
  - (* sub *) exact IH1.
Qed.

Proof.
  intros G e1 e2 A H. induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf

    | G0 e A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar

    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr

  - apply sub_ax; auto.

  - apply sub_var_refl with (e := e1); auto. apply sub_wf in Hprem; auto.

    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr

Proof.

Lemma sub_second_var_diag : forall G e x A,

Proof.
  intros G e x A H.

    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];

  e = trm_star \/ exists x, e = trm_var_f x.
Proof.

  - subst e2. apply IHsub1. reflexivity.
Qed.

    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar

Lemma subenv_refl : forall G, subenv G G.
Proof. intros G y b H. exact H. Qed.

Lemma wf_binds_type : forall G x e A,
  wf G -> binds x (bind_sub e A) G -> sub G A A trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G. induction G as [| G' y b IH] using env_ind.
  - intros x e A Hwf Hb. apply binds_empty_inv in Hb. destruct Hb.
  - intros x e A Hwf Hb.
    destruct b as [eb Ab].
    destruct (@wf_cons_inv G' y eb Ab Hwf) as [Hwf' [He' [HA' HyG]]].
    apply binds_push_inv in Hb.
    destruct Hb as [[Hxy He] | [Hxy Hb']].
    + subst y. injection He as Hbe HAb. subst eb Ab.
      eapply sub_weaken_push; [ exact Hwf | apply subenv_refl | exact HyG | exact HA' ].
    + eapply sub_weaken_push; [ exact Hwf | apply subenv_refl | exact HyG | ].
      eapply IH; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hb' ].
Qed.

   type.  This complements [wf_binds_type] and is what makes a context's
   stored definitions usable under weakening.                            *)

  wf G -> binds x (bind_sub e A) G -> sub G e e A.
Proof.
  intros G. induction G as [| G' y b IH] using env_ind.
  - intros x e A Hwf Hb. apply binds_empty_inv in Hb. destruct Hb.
  - intros x e A Hwf Hb.
    destruct b as [eb Ab].
    destruct (@wf_cons_inv G' y eb Ab Hwf) as [Hwf' [He' [HA' HyG]]].
    apply binds_push_inv in Hb.
    destruct Hb as [[Hxy He] | [Hxy Hb']].
    + subst y. injection He as Hbe HAb. subst eb Ab.
      eapply sub_weaken_push; [ exact Hwf | apply subenv_refl | exact HyG | exact He' ].
    + eapply sub_weaken_push; [ exact Hwf | apply subenv_refl | exact HyG | ].
      eapply IH; [ exact Hwf' | exact Hb' ].
Qed.

Inductive sub_chain : env -> trm -> trm -> Prop :=
 | sub_chain_refl : forall G P, sub_chain G P P
 | sub_chain_step : forall G P Q R,
     sub G P Q trm_star -> sub_chain G Q R -> sub_chain G P R.

Lemma sub_chain_append : forall G P Q,
  sub_chain G P Q -> forall R, sub G Q R trm_star -> sub_chain G P R.
Proof.
  intros G P Q H. induction H as [G0 P0 | G0 P0 Q0 R0 hstep hrest IH].
  - intros S hS. apply sub_chain_step with (Q := S);
      [ exact hS | apply sub_chain_refl ].
  - intros S hS. apply sub_chain_step with (Q := Q0);
      [ exact hstep | apply (IH S); exact hS ].
Qed.


(* A diagonal typing of an abstraction at [P] passes through a chain of
   product widenings from its canonical product [prod d D B0].  This is
   the structural decomposition needed to reason about widened abstract
   typings.                                                               *)

Lemma sub_abs_diag_chain : forall G d D b P,
  sub G (trm_abs d D b) (trm_abs d D b) P ->
  exists B0, sub_chain G (trm_prod d D B0) P.
Proof.
  intros G d D b P H.
  remember (trm_abs d D b) as lhs eqn:El.
  remember (trm_abs d D b) as rhs eqn:Er.
  revert d D b El Er.
  induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros d D b El Er.
  all: try (exfalso; congruence).
  - (* sub_var_trans *) exact (IHprem d D b El Er).
  - (* sub_abs *)
    assert (Heq : trm_abs e1 A0 e2' = trm_abs d D b)
      by (rewrite El; exact Er).
    injection Heq as Hd HD Hb. subst.
    exists B. apply sub_chain_refl.
  - (* sub_sub *)
    destruct (IH1 d D b El Er) as [B0 Hc].
    exists B0. eapply sub_chain_append; [ exact Hc | exact h2 ].
Qed.


(* Full inversion of a diagonal abstraction typing: it returns the
   canonical codomain family [B0], the abstraction body's self-typing and
   the codomain's self-typing in the canonical binder context, together
   with a widening chain from the canonical product to the result type.
   This is the decomposition used by the beta case of subject reduction. *)

Lemma sub_abs_diag_inv : forall G d D b P,
  sub G (trm_abs d D b) (trm_abs d D b) P ->
  exists L B0,
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
       sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (b ^ x) (b ^ x) (B0 ^ x)) /\
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
       sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (B0 ^ x) (B0 ^ x) trm_star) /\
    sub_chain G (trm_prod d D B0) P.
Proof.
  intros G d D b P H.
  dependent induction H.
  - (* sub_abs *)
    exists L, B. repeat split;
      [ exact H1 | exact H3 | apply sub_chain_refl ].
  - (* sub_sub *)
    destruct (IHsub1 d D b eq_refl eq_refl) as [L [B0 [Hbod [Hcod Hc]]]].
    exists L, B0. repeat split; [ exact Hbod | exact Hcod | ].
    eapply sub_chain_append; [ exact Hc | exact H0 ].
Qed.


(* Non-diagonal inversion of an abstraction typing: two abstractions with
   the same annotation.  Returns the canonical codomain, the (possibly
   non-diagonal) body relation, the codomain self-typing, and the widening
   chain.  This supplies the data for the abstraction case of the
   same-type composition lemma.                                          *)

Lemma sub_abs_inv : forall G d D b1 b2 P,
  sub G (trm_abs d D b1) (trm_abs d D b2) P ->
  exists L B0,
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
       sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (b1 ^ x) (b2 ^ x) (B0 ^ x)) /\
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
       sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (B0 ^ x) (B0 ^ x) trm_star) /\
    sub_chain G (trm_prod d D B0) P.

  intros G d D b1 b2 P H.
  dependent induction H.
  - (* sub_abs *)
    exists L, B. repeat split;
      [ exact H1 | exact H3 | apply sub_chain_refl ].
  - (* sub_sub *)
    destruct (IHsub1 d D b1 b2 eq_refl eq_refl) as [L [B0 [Hbod [Hcod Hc]]]].
    exists L, B0. repeat split; [ exact Hbod | exact Hcod | ].
    eapply sub_chain_append; [ exact Hc | exact H0 ].
Qed.

Proof.
  intros G e1 e2 A H.
  induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
Lemma sub_chain_single : forall G P Q,
  sub G P Q trm_star -> sub_chain G P Q.
Proof.
  intros. apply sub_chain_step with (Q := Q);
    [ exact H | apply sub_chain_refl ].
Qed.

Lemma sub_chain_trans : forall G P Q,
  sub_chain G P Q -> forall R, sub_chain G Q R -> sub_chain G P R.
Proof.
  intros G P Q H. induction H as [G0 P0 | G0 P0 Q0 R0 hstep hrest IH].
  - intros R hR. exact hR.
  - intros R hR. apply sub_chain_step with (Q := Q0);
      [ exact hstep | apply (IH R hR) ].
Qed.

Lemma sub_chain_step_inv : forall G P Q,
  sub_chain G P Q -> P <> Q ->
  exists R, sub G P R trm_star /\ sub_chain G R Q.
Proof.
  intros G P Q H. destruct H as [G0 P0 | G0 P0 Q0 R0 hstep hrest].
  - intro Hne. exfalso. apply Hne. reflexivity.
  - intro Hne2. exists Q0. split; assumption.
Qed.

(* Single-step same-domain collapse: a product widening between products
   with the same domain exposes its codomain-family relation directly in
   that domain's binder context.                                           *)

Lemma sub_prod_same_domain_codom : forall G d D Bv B,
  sub G (trm_prod d D Bv) (trm_prod d D B) trm_star ->
  exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
    sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (Bv ^ x) (B ^ x) trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G d D Bv B H.
  destruct (sub_prod_full_gen H eq_refl eq_refl)
    as [H1 [H2 [H3 [H4 [H5 [H6 H7]]]]]].
  exact H5.
Qed.

(* Domain component relations of a product widening (monotonicity). *)

Lemma sub_prod_domain_relations : forall G d D Bv e A B,
  sub G (trm_prod d D Bv) (trm_prod e A B) trm_star ->
  sub G A D trm_star /\ sub G e d D.
Proof.
  intros G d D Bv e A B H.
  destruct (sub_prod_full_gen H eq_refl eq_refl)
    as [H1 [H2 [H3 [H4 [H5 [H6 H7]]]]]].
  split; assumption.
Qed.

(* A type that is self-typed at [star] is locally closed. *)

Lemma sub_lc_type_star : forall G A, sub G A A trm_star -> lc_trm A.
Proof.
  intros G A H. destruct (sub_lc_terms H) as [HA _]. exact HA.
Qed.

(* Source codomain self-typing of a same-domain product widening, in the
   common domain's binder context.                                       *)

Lemma sub_prod_same_domain_self : forall G d D Bv B,
  sub G (trm_prod d D Bv) (trm_prod d D B) trm_star ->
  exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
    sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (Bv ^ x) (Bv ^ x) trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G d D Bv B H.
  destruct (sub_prod_full_gen H eq_refl eq_refl)
    as [H1 [H2 [H3 [H4 [H5 [H6 H7]]]]]].
  exact H4.
Qed.

(* All components of a typing whose type is self-typed at [star] are
   locally closed.                                                      *)

Lemma sub_all_lc : forall G e1 e2 A,
  sub G e1 e2 A -> sub G A A trm_star ->
  lc_trm e1 /\ lc_trm e2 /\ lc_trm A.
Proof.
  intros G e1 e2 A H HA.
  destruct (sub_lc_terms H) as [H1 H2].
  pose proof (sub_lc_type_star HA) as H3.
  auto.
Qed.

(* [top] is a right supertype at any supertype of a type at which the term
   is self-typed.                                                       *)

Lemma sub_top_lift : forall G e A B,
  sub G e e A -> sub G A B trm_star -> sub G e trm_top B.
Proof.
  intros G e A B He HAB. apply sub_top.
  eapply sub_sub; [ exact He | exact HAB ].
Qed.

(* A bound variable is below [top] at its binding type. *)

Lemma sub_var_top : forall G x e A,
  wf G -> binds x (bind_sub e A) G -> sub G (trm_var_f x) trm_top A.
Proof.
  intros G x e A Hwf Hb. apply sub_top.
  apply sub_var_refl with (e := e); assumption.
Qed.

   widening chain.                                                      *)

Lemma sub_abs_inv_full : forall G d D b1 b2 P,
  sub G (trm_abs d D b1) (trm_abs d D b2) P ->
  sub G d d D /\
  sub G D D trm_star /\
  exists L B0,
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
       sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (b1 ^ x) (b2 ^ x) (B0 ^ x)) /\
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
       sub (G & x ~ bind_sub d D) (B0 ^ x) (B0 ^ x) trm_star) /\
    sub_chain G (trm_prod d D B0) P.
Proof.
  intros G d D b1 b2 P H.
  destruct (sub_abs_wf_ctx_gen H eq_refl eq_refl) as [Hd HD].
  split; [ exact Hd | split; [ exact HD | exact (sub_abs_inv H) ] ].

  sub G (trm_prod e A B) (trm_prod e A B) trm_star.
Proof.
  intros L G e A B HeeA HAA Hbody.
  apply (sub_prod L G e A B e A B);

    | exact HeeA | exact HeeA ].
Qed.

(* Chaining two type-level widenings on the type of a judgment. *)

Lemma sub_sub_trans : forall G e1 e2 A B C,
  sub G e1 e2 A -> sub G A B trm_star -> sub G B C trm_star ->
  sub G e1 e2 C.
Proof.
  intros G e1 e2 A B C H HAB HBC.
  eapply sub_sub; [ | exact HBC ].
  eapply sub_sub; [ exact H | exact HAB ].
Qed.

(* Diagonal abstraction introduction (specialized [sub_abs] with the same
   body on both sides).                                                  *)

Lemma sub_abs_self : forall L G e A b B,
  sub G e e A -> sub G A A trm_star ->

  (forall x, x \notin L ->

  sub G (trm_abs e A b) (trm_abs e A b) (trm_prod e A B).
Proof.
  intros L G e A b B He HAA Hbody Hcod.
  apply (sub_abs L G e A b b B); assumption.
Qed.

Lemma sub_sub_trans : forall G e1 e2 A B C,
  sub G e1 e2 A -> sub G A B trm_star -> sub G B C trm_star ->
  sub G e1 e2 C.
Proof.
  intros G e1 e2 A B C H HAB HBC.
  eapply sub_sub; [ | exact HBC ].
  eapply sub_sub; [ exact H | exact HAB ].
Qed.

Lemma sub_abs_self : forall L G e A b B,
  sub G e e A -> sub G A A trm_star ->
  (forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub e A) (b ^ x) (b ^ x) (B ^ x)) ->
  (forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub e A) (B ^ x) (B ^ x) trm_star) ->
  sub G (trm_abs e A b) (trm_abs e A b) (trm_prod e A B).
Proof.
  intros L G e A b B He HAA Hbody Hcod.
  apply (sub_abs L G e A b b B); assumption.
Qed.

From TLC Require Import LibLN.

Inductive trm : Set :=
 | trm_var_b (_:nat)
 | trm_var_f (x5:var)
 | trm_star : trm
 | trm_top : trm
 | trm_app (e1:trm) (e2:trm)
 | trm_abs (e1:trm) (A:trm) (e2:trm)
 | trm_prod (e:trm) (A:trm) (B:trm)
 | trm_castup (A:trm) (e:trm)
 | trm_castdn (e:trm)
 | trm_anno (e:trm) (A:trm)  .

Inductive binding : Set :=
 | bind_sub (e:trm) (A:trm)  .

Definition env := LibEnv.env binding.

Fixpoint open_trm_wrt_trm_rec (k:nat) (e_5:trm) (e__6:trm) {struct e__6}: trm :=
  match e__6 with
  | (trm_var_b nat) => If (k = nat) then e_5 else (trm_var_b nat)
  | (trm_var_f x5) => trm_var_f x5
  | trm_star => trm_star
  | trm_top => trm_top
  | (trm_app e1 e2) => trm_app (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 e1) (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 e2)
  | (trm_abs e1 A e2) => trm_abs (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 e1) (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 A) (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec (S k) e_5 e2)
  | (trm_prod e A B) => trm_prod (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 e) (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 A) (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec (S k) e_5 B)
  | (trm_castup A e) => trm_castup (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 A) (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 e)
  | (trm_castdn e) => trm_castdn (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 e)
  | (trm_anno e A) => trm_anno (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 e) (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e_5 A)
end.

Definition open_binding_wrt_trm_rec (k:nat) (e5:trm) (b5:binding) : binding :=
  match b5 with
  | (bind_sub e A) => bind_sub (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e5 e) (open_trm_wrt_trm_rec k e5 A)
end.

Definition open_binding_wrt_trm e5 b5 := open_binding_wrt_trm_rec 0 b5 e5.

Definition open_trm_wrt_trm e_5 e__6 := open_trm_wrt_trm_rec 0 e__6 e_5.

Inductive lc_trm : trm -> Prop :=
 | lc_trm_var_f : forall (x5:var),
     (lc_trm (trm_var_f x5))
 | lc_trm_star :
     (lc_trm trm_star)
 | lc_trm_top :
     (lc_trm trm_top)
 | lc_trm_app : forall (e1 e2:trm),
     (lc_trm e1) ->
     (lc_trm e2) ->
     (lc_trm (trm_app e1 e2))
 | lc_trm_abs : forall (L:vars) (e1 A e2:trm),
     (lc_trm e1) ->
     (lc_trm A) ->
      ( forall x5 , x5 \notin  L  -> lc_trm  ( open_trm_wrt_trm e2 (trm_var_f x5) )  )  ->
     (lc_trm (trm_abs e1 A e2))
 | lc_trm_prod : forall (L:vars) (e A B:trm),
     (lc_trm e) ->
     (lc_trm A) ->
      ( forall x5 , x5 \notin  L  -> lc_trm  ( open_trm_wrt_trm B (trm_var_f x5) )  )  ->
     (lc_trm (trm_prod e A B))
 | lc_trm_castup : forall (A e:trm),
     (lc_trm A) ->
     (lc_trm e) ->
     (lc_trm (trm_castup A e))
 | lc_trm_castdn : forall (e:trm),
     (lc_trm e) ->
     (lc_trm (trm_castdn e))
 | lc_trm_anno : forall (e A:trm),
     (lc_trm e) ->
     (lc_trm A) ->
     (lc_trm (trm_anno e A)).

Inductive lc_binding : binding -> Prop :=
 | lc_bind_sub : forall (e A:trm),
     (lc_trm e) ->
     (lc_trm A) ->
     (lc_binding (bind_sub e A)).

Fixpoint fv_trm (e_5:trm) : vars :=
  match e_5 with
  | (trm_var_b nat) => \{}
  | (trm_var_f x5) => \{x5}
  | trm_star => \{}
  | trm_top => \{}
  | (trm_app e1 e2) => (fv_trm e1) \u (fv_trm e2)
  | (trm_abs e1 A e2) => (fv_trm e1) \u (fv_trm A) \u (fv_trm e2)
  | (trm_prod e A B) => (fv_trm e) \u (fv_trm A) \u (fv_trm B)
  | (trm_castup A e) => (fv_trm A) \u (fv_trm e)
  | (trm_castdn e) => (fv_trm e)
  | (trm_anno e A) => (fv_trm e) \u (fv_trm A)
end.

Definition fv_binding (b5:binding) : vars :=
  match b5 with
  | (bind_sub e A) => (fv_trm e) \u (fv_trm A)
end.

Fixpoint subst_trm (e_5:trm) (y5:var) (e__6:trm) {struct e__6} : trm :=
  match e__6 with
  | (trm_var_b nat) => trm_var_b nat
  | (trm_var_f x5) => (If x5 = y5 then e_5 else (trm_var_f x5))
  | trm_star => trm_star
  | trm_top => trm_top
  | (trm_app e1 e2) => trm_app (subst_trm e_5 y5 e1) (subst_trm e_5 y5 e2)
  | (trm_abs e1 A e2) => trm_abs (subst_trm e_5 y5 e1) (subst_trm e_5 y5 A) (subst_trm e_5 y5 e2)
  | (trm_prod e A B) => trm_prod (subst_trm e_5 y5 e) (subst_trm e_5 y5 A) (subst_trm e_5 y5 B)
  | (trm_castup A e) => trm_castup (subst_trm e_5 y5 A) (subst_trm e_5 y5 e)
  | (trm_castdn e) => trm_castdn (subst_trm e_5 y5 e)
  | (trm_anno e A) => trm_anno (subst_trm e_5 y5 e) (subst_trm e_5 y5 A)
end.

Definition subst_binding (e5:trm) (y5:var) (b5:binding) : binding :=
  match b5 with
  | (bind_sub e A) => bind_sub (subst_trm e5 y5 e) (subst_trm e5 y5 A)
end.

Inductive reduct : trm -> trm -> Prop :=
====
 | ivalue_top :
     ivalue trm_top
 | ivalue_var : forall (x5:var),
     ivalue (trm_var_f x5)
 | ivalue_app : forall (e1 e2:trm),
     lc_trm e2 ->
     ivalue e1 ->
     ivalue (trm_app e1 e2)
 | ivalue_castdn : forall (e:trm),
     ivalue e ->
     ivalue (trm_castdn e).

Inductive value : trm -> Prop :=
 | value_star :
     value trm_star
 | value_ivalue : forall (e:trm),
     ivalue e ->
     value e
 | value_abs : forall (e1 A e2:trm),
     lc_trm e1 ->
     lc_trm A ->
     lc_trm (trm_abs e1 A e2) ->
     value (trm_abs e1 A e2)
 | value_prod : forall (e A B:trm),
     lc_trm e ->
     lc_trm A ->
     lc_trm (trm_prod e A B) ->
     value (trm_prod e A B)
 | value_castup : forall (A e:trm),
     lc_trm A ->
     lc_trm e ->
     value (trm_castup A e).

Lemma sub_prod_idx_example : forall x,
  sub (empty & x ~ bind_sub trm_star trm_star)
      (trm_prod trm_star trm_star trm_star)
      (trm_prod (trm_var_f x) trm_star trm_star)
      trm_star.
Proof.
  intros x.
  set (G := empty & x ~ bind_sub trm_star trm_star).

  { unfold G. apply wf_cons.
    - apply sub_ax. apply wf_nil.
    - apply sub_ax. apply wf_nil.
    - rewrite dom_empty. apply notin_empty. }
  assert (Hx : sub G (trm_var_f x) (trm_var_f x) trm_star).
  { apply sub_var_refl with (e := trm_star); [ exact Hwf | apply binds_tail ]. }

  { eapply sub_var_trans; [ apply binds_tail | apply sub_ax; exact Hwf ]. }
  assert (Hax : sub G trm_star trm_star trm_star).
  { apply sub_ax. exact Hwf. }

                   (trm_var_f x) trm_star trm_star).

  - (* p2 *) exact Hxs.
  - (* p3 *) exact Hax.
  - (* h4 *) intros y Hy. apply sub_ax.
    apply wf_cons.
    + exact Hax.
    + exact Hax.
    + unfold G; rewrite dom_push, dom_empty; apply notin_union; split; [ exact Hy | apply notin_empty ].
  - (* h5 *) intros y Hy. apply sub_ax.
    apply wf_cons.
    + exact Hx.
    + exact Hax.
    + unfold G; rewrite dom_push, dom_empty; apply notin_union; split; [ exact Hy | apply notin_empty ].
  - (* p6 *) exact Hax.
  - (* p7 *) exact Hx.
Qed.

(* Full component extraction for product subtyping.  Since [sub_sub]
   preserves both terms, any derivation of a product-to-product judgment
   bottoms out in a single [sub_prod] between the very same endpoint
   products, so all the [sub_prod] premises are available for the
   endpoints.  This is used to recover the domain term/type relations and
   the codomain family relation of a product widening.                     *)

Lemma sub_prod_full_gen : forall G d e T,
  sub G d e T ->
  forall p q r p' q' r',
    d = trm_prod p q r -> e = trm_prod p' q' r' ->
    (sub G q' q trm_star) /\
    (sub G p' p q) /\
    (sub G q q trm_star) /\
    (exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
        sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p q) (r ^ x) (r ^ x) trm_star) /\
    (exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
        sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p' q') (r ^ x) (r' ^ x) trm_star) /\
    (sub G p p q) /\
    (sub G p' p' q').
Proof.
  intros G d e T H.
  induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros p q r p' q' r' Ed Ee; try discriminate Ed.
  - (* sub_top: the right component is [top] *)
    discriminate Ee.
  - (* sub_prod *)
    injection Ed as He HA HB. injection Ee as He' HA' HB'. subst.
    split. exact h1.
    split. exact h2.
    split. exact h3.
    split. exists L. exact h4.
    split. exists L. exact h5.
    split. exact h6.
    exact h7.
  - (* sub_sub: terms are preserved *)
    exact (IH1 p q r p' q' r' Ed Ee).
Qed.

(* Codomain-family relation of a product widening, in the target product's
   binder context.  This is the [sub_prod] premise needed to advance a
   codomain family along a widening step.                                  *)

Lemma sub_prod_codom_gen : forall G p q r p' q' r',
  sub G (trm_prod p q r) (trm_prod p' q' r') trm_star ->
  exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
    sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p' q') (r ^ x) (r' ^ x) trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G p q r p' q' r' H.
  destruct (sub_prod_full_gen H eq_refl eq_refl)
    as [H1 [H2 [H3 [H4 [H5 [H6 H7]]]]]].
  exact H5.
Qed.

(* The packaged data of a single product-widening step: domain type and
   term relations, both domain self-typings, the source codomain
   self-typing, and the codomain-family relation in the target binder
   context.  These are exactly the [sub_prod] premises needed to advance
   a codomain family (and hence an opened abstraction body) along one
   step of a widening chain.                                              *)

Lemma sub_prod_step : forall G p q r p' q' r',
  sub G (trm_prod p q r) (trm_prod p' q' r') trm_star ->
  (sub G q' q trm_star) /\
  (sub G p' p q) /\
  (sub G q q trm_star) /\
  (sub G p p q) /\
  (sub G p' p' q') /\
  (exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p q) (r ^ x) (r ^ x) trm_star) /\
  (exists L, forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub p' q') (r ^ x) (r' ^ x) trm_star).
Proof.
  intros G p q r p' q' r' H.
  destruct (sub_prod_full_gen H eq_refl eq_refl)
    as [H1 [H2 [H3 [H4 [H5 [H6 H7]]]]]].
  split. exact H1.
  split. exact H2.
  split. exact H3.
  split. exact H6.
  split. exact H7.
  split. exact H4.
  exact H5.
Qed.

(* Both binder contexts associated with the two endpoints of a product
   widening are well formed (for a fresh variable), so the target-context
   codomain relation of [sub_prod_step] can be used directly.              *)

Lemma wf_of_prod_step : forall G p q r p' q' r',
  sub G (trm_prod p q r) (trm_prod p' q' r') trm_star ->
  forall x, x # G ->
    wf (G & x ~ bind_sub p q) /\ wf (G & x ~ bind_sub p' q').
Proof.
  intros G p q r p' q' r' H x Hx.
  destruct (sub_prod_step H) as [H1 [H2 [H3 [H6 [H7 [H4 H5]]]]]].
  split.
  - apply wf_cons; [ exact H6 | exact H3 | exact Hx ].
  - apply wf_cons.
    + exact H7.
    + apply sub_left in H1. exact H1.
    + exact Hx.
Qed.

(* Inversion data for a typing of an abstraction pair: regardless of the
   result type (and of [sub_sub] wrappers), the domain term is self-typed
   at the domain type and the domain type is self-typed at [star].  This
   is exactly what is needed to form the body's binder context.            *)

Lemma sub_abs_wf_ctx_gen : forall G d e T,
  sub G d e T ->
  forall a0 D b b',
    d = trm_abs a0 D b -> e = trm_abs a0 D b' ->
    sub G a0 a0 D /\ sub G D D trm_star.
Proof.
  intros G d e T H.
  induction H as
    [ G0 Hwf
    | G0 x5 A0 e0 Hwf Hb
    | G0 x5 e2 A0 e1 Hb Hprem IHprem
    | G0 e0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | G0 A0 Hprem IHprem
    | L G0 e1 A0 e2 e2' B h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hbody IHbody hbs IHbstar
    | G0 e1 A0 e2 C e3 B h1 IH1 h2 IH2
    | L G0 e A0 B e' A' B' h1 IH1 h2 IH2 h3 IH3 h4 IH4 h5 IH5 h6 IH6 h7 IH7
    | G0 B e1 e2 A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 hr
    | G0 e1 e2 B A0 h1 IH1 h2 IH2 ];
  intros a0 D b b' Ed Ee; try discriminate Ed.
  - (* sub_top: right component is [top] *)
    discriminate Ee.
  - (* sub_abs: the annotations are forced by the two terms *)
    injection Ed as He1 HD Hb. injection Ee as He1' HD' Hb'.
    subst. split; [ exact h1 | exact h2 ].
  - (* sub_sub: terms are preserved *)
    exact (IH1 a0 D b b' Ed Ee).
Qed.

Lemma wf_abs_body_ctx : forall G a0 D b b' T,
  sub G (trm_abs a0 D b) (trm_abs a0 D b') T ->
  forall x, x # G -> wf (G & x ~ bind_sub a0 D).
Proof.
  intros G a0 D b b' T H x Hx.
  destruct (sub_abs_wf_ctx_gen H eq_refl eq_refl) as [H1 H2].
  apply wf_cons; [ exact H1 | exact H2 | exact Hx ].
Qed.

(* Scope of bindings in a well-formed environment: the free variables of
   the term and type components of every binding lie in the environment
   domain.  This is the key fact that lets a fresh binder name be treated
   as absent from all inherited bindings.                                *)

  wf (G & x ~ bind_sub e A) -> wf G /\ sub G e e A /\ sub G A A trm_star /\ x # G.

    split; [exact H1|].
    split; [exact H2|exact H3].

Lemma sub_sub_trans : forall G e1 e2 A B C,
  sub G e1 e2 A -> sub G A B trm_star -> sub G B C trm_star ->
  sub G e1 e2 C.
Proof.
  intros G e1 e2 A B C H HAB HBC.
  eapply sub_sub; [ | exact HBC ].
  eapply sub_sub; [ exact H | exact HAB ].
Qed.

(* Diagonal abstraction introduction (specialized [sub_abs] with the same
   body on both sides).                                                  *)

Lemma sub_abs_self : forall L G e A b B,
  sub G e e A -> sub G A A trm_star ->
  (forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub e A) (b ^ x) (b ^ x) (B ^ x)) ->
  (forall x, x \notin L ->
     sub (G & x ~ bind_sub e A) (B ^ x) (B ^ x) trm_star) ->
  sub G (trm_abs e A b) (trm_abs e A b) (trm_prod e A B).
Proof.
  intros L G e A b B He HAA Hbody Hcod.
  apply (sub_abs L G e A b b B); assumption.
Qed.

(* Diagonal application introduction (specialized [sub_app]). *)

Lemma sub_app_self : forall G f a e B C,
  sub G f f (trm_prod e B C) -> sub G a e B ->
  sub G (trm_app f a) (trm_app f a) (C ^^ a).
Proof.
  intros G f a e B C Hf Ha.
  apply (sub_app G f a f C e B); assumption.
Qed.

(* Definitional distribution of substitution over term constructors. *)

Lemma subst_trm_app : forall v x a b,
  subst_trm v x (trm_app a b) = trm_app (subst_trm v x a) (subst_trm v x b).
